subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Why living on the edge is popular
question:
The choices we make on a daily basis—wearing a seatbelt, lifting heavy objects correctly or purposely staying out of any dangerous situation—can either ensure our safety or bring about potentially harmful circumstances.
You and I need to make a decision that we are going to get our lives in order. Exercising self-control, self-discipline and establishing boundaries and borders in our lives are some of the most important things we can do. A life without discipline is one that’s filled with carelessness.
We can think it’s kind of exciting to live life on the edge. We like the image of “Yeah! That’s me! Living on the edge! Woo-hoo!” It’s become a popular way to look at life. But if you see, even highways have lines, which provide margins for our safety while we’re driving. If we go over one side, we’ll go into the ditch. If we cross over the line in the middle, we could get killed. And we like those lines because they help to keep us safe. Sometimes we don’t even realize how lines help to keep us safe.
I’m not proud of this, but for the first 20 years of my life at work, I ignored my limits. I felt horrible, physically, most of the time. I used to tell myself “I know I have limits and that I’ve reached them, but I’m going to ignore them and see if or how long I can get by with it.” I ran to doctors, trying to make myself feel better through pills, vitamins, natural stuff and anything I could get my hands on. Some of the doctors would tell me, “It’s just stress.” That just made me mad. I thought stress meant you don’t like what you do or can’t handle life, and I love what I do. But I kept pushing myself, traveling, doing speaking engagements and so on— simply exhausting myself.
Finally, I understood I was living an unsustainable life and needed to make some changes in my outlook and lifestyle.
You and I don’t have to be like everyone else or keep up with anyone else. Each of us needs to be exactly the way we are, and we don’t have to apologize for it. We’re not all alike and we need to find a comfort zone in which we can enjoy our lives instead of making ourselves sick with an overload of stress and pressure.
The reason why living on the edge has become popular, is because of the
options: (D) strong tendency to stay within our limits.
explanation: The writer says people find it exciting to live life on the edge. That excitement comes from a constant craving for thrill and something different from an ordinary, disciplined life.

Choose the option that best captures the central idea of the passage from the given quotes.
(1) It’s all about quality of life and finding a happy balance between work and friends. --Philip Green
(2) To go beyond is as wrong as to fall short. --Confucius
(3) Life is like riding a bicycle. To keep your balance you must keep moving. --Albert Einstein

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Word meaning a style of cooking
question:
(1) As the family finally sets off from home after many arguments there is a moment of lull as the car takes off. “Alright, so where are we going for dinner now?” asks the one at the driving wheel. What follows is a chaos as multiple voices make as many suggestions.
(2) By the time order is restored and a decision is arrived at, tempers have risen, feelings injured and there is at least one person grumbling.
(3) Twenty years ago, you would step out of home, decision of meal and venue already made with no arguments or opposition and everybody looked forward to the meal with equal enthusiasm. The decision was made by the head of the family and the others fell in line. Today every member of the family has a say in every decision which also promotes a sense of togetherness and bonding.
(4) We empower our kids to take their own decisions from a very early age. We ask them the cuisine they prefer, the movie they want to see, the holiday they wish to go on and the subjects they wish to study.
(5) It’s a closely connected world out there where children consult and guide each other. A parent’s well meaning advice can sound like nothing more than unnecessary preaching. How then do we reach our children through all the conflicting views and make the voice of reason be heard ? Children today question choices and prefer to go with the flow.
(6) What then is the best path to take? I would say the most important thing one can do is to listen. Listen to your children and their silences. Ensure that you keep some time aside for them, insist that they share their stories with you. Step into their world. It is not as complicated as it sounds; just a daily half an hour of the quality time would do the trick.
The word which means the same as ‘a style or method of cooking’ in paragraph 4 is :
explanation: Paragraph 4 says parents ask children the cuisine they prefer. Cuisine means a style or method of cooking, while a gourmet is a person who enjoys fine food.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
(1) The difference in the ways of thinking and perception of the people of two different generations, which results in behavioural differences and sometimes, conflict among them is usually called generation gap.
(2) Generation gap is generally seen in the family between parents and their children. It is not only because of the gap in age, but also because of the way parents react to a particular situation. Children being very young and immature do not understand the way of thinking of their parents. In many cases, the parents, even if they are mature, do not identify with the changing values and thinking patterns of the modern world. This creates a communication gap between these two generations.
(3) Generation gap between parents and children is mostly caused by parents themselves. They do not talk openly to their children and take no part in solving their problems. This behaviour gives the impression about parents being authoritative persons, because they only dictate without understanding the problems faced by their children. As a result, the children become mentally isolated from their parents. Some parents become so busy with their work that they do not spend quality time with their family, which makes them completely unaware of how their children are growing, what kind of mentality is being developed in them, and so on. This ultimately creates a gap between them. They only realize it when it is too late.
(4) Changes in technology have led to the generation gap in this modern world. Children tend to spend most of their time with their mobile phones and are so busy with social media, that they do not discuss their problems with their parents. The Internet provides solutions to most of the worldly problems. So children, instead of contacting their own parents, take the help of the Internet in case of any problem, thus again reducing the communication, leading to generation gap between them.
(5) The generation gap has greatly increased these days because the time is changing fast and people find it difficult to deal with this change. To overcome this problem, parents should show interest in all matters of their children and deal with them positively instead of just scolding them and leaving them alone to deal with their problems. Giving time to the children, having open communication, and allowing the child to feel free and not be under any kind of pressure, will eventually reduce the generation gap to a tolerable extent.
What is meant by the word, ‘particular’ ? (para 2)
explanation: Paragraph 2 speaks of the way parents react to a particular situation. Here particular refers to one specific situation rather than a usual or normal one.

question:
The Road to Success
1. The Road to success is not straight; there is a curve called failure, a loop called confusion, speed bumps called friends, caution lights called family, and you will have flats called jobs. But, if you have a spare called determination, an engine called perseverance, insurance called faith, and a driver called God, you will make it to a place called success!
2. In spite of all our planning and preparation, unexpected challenges are certain to arise. The bumps in the road are unavoidable, but you’ll never get to your destination if you aren’t willing to drive over them. The difference between a disaster and triumph lies in whether or not you’re prepared and willing to weather the storm. If you’re ready, those bumps will become stepping-stones.
3. The key thing to realize is that working harder is same as working smarter. How do you work smarter? You just need to have the right skills. People want improved circumstances and better life without an improved self. They want victory without paying the price or making efforts. It really cannot happen without the other. Any improvements that have not been generated by improving yourself are superficial and short-lived. If you want to have a better future, you have to change yourself. Stop worrying about the various challenges that will come your way. Just believe in yourself and use them as stepping-stones.
4. “Success” is getting whatever you want out of life without violating the rights of others.” It is not an accident. Success is the result of our attitude and our attitude is a choice. Hence success is a matter of choice and not chance.
5. Today success represents a holistic and positive attitude to life. Attitude is everything. Success is not restricted within some kind of brick and mortar premises. It assumes the individuality of a complete act executed with perfection; material achievements do not define life. We don’t remember sports stars for the products they endorse but the spirit of achievement they represent. In the abundance of positive attitude underline the grandeur of a truly rewarding rich life.
6. Success can be measured from two standpoints—the external and the internal. Externally it is the measure of a job well done and recognition. Internally it the feeling of achievement and wholeness derived from the completion of a task or fulfillment of desire.
The synonym of ‘victory’ as given in paragraph 2 is ____________
explanation: Paragraph 2 says the difference between a disaster and triumph lies in being prepared. Triumph means a great victory or success, so it is the synonym of victory.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
1. Have you ever failed at something so miserably that the thought of attempting to do it again was the last thing you wanted to do?
2. If your answer is yes, then you are “not a robot.” Unlike robots, we human beings have feelings, emotions, and dreams. We are all meant to grow and stretch despite our circumstances and our limitations. Flourishing and trying to make our dreams come true is great when life is going our way. But what happens when it’s not? What happens when you fail despite all of your hard work? Do you stay down and accept the defeat or do you get up again and again until you are satisfied? If you have a tendency to persevere and keep going then you have what experts call, grit.
3. Falling down or failing is one of the most agonizing, embarrassing, and scariest human experiences. But it is also one of the most educational, empowering, and essential parts of living a successful and fulfilling life. Did you know that perseverance (grit) is one of the seven qualities that have been described as the keys to personal success and betterment in society? The other six are: curiosity, gratitude, optimism, self-control, social intelligence, and zest. Thomas Edison is a model for grit for trying 1,000 plus times to invent the light bulb. If you are reading this with the lights on in your room, you know well he succeeded. When asked why he kept going despite his hundreds of failures, he merely stated that what he had been not failures. They were hundreds of ways not to create a light bulb. This statement not only revealed his grit but also his optimism for looking at the bright side
4. Grit can be learned to help you become more successful. One of the techniques that help is mindfulness. Mindfulness is a practice that helps the individual stay in the moment by bringing awareness of his or her experience without judgment. This practice has been used to quiet the noise of their fears and doubts. Through this simple practice of mindfulness, individuals have the ability to stop the self-sabotaging downward spiral of hopelessness, despair, and frustration.
5. What did you do to overcome the negative and self-sabotaging feelings of failure? Reflect on what you did, and try to use those same powerful resources to help you today.
While inventing the light bulb, Thomas Edison had failed ________
explanation: Paragraph 3 says Thomas Edison is a model for grit for trying 1,000 plus times to invent the light bulb. Each of those attempts that did not work counted as a failure before he finally succeeded.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
(1) It is an indisputable fact that the world has gone too far with the innovation of new technologies such as mobile phones, the internet and so on, due to which people are able to tour the cosmos virtually sitting at one place using their smart devices or other technological gadgets. Though mobile internet access is oftentimes hurried and short, it can still provide common internet features like alerts, weather data, emails, search engines, instant messages, and game and music downloading.
(2) Due to the easy access of smart phones, communication has been very effective and instant. People are able to convey their message all around the globe to their loved ones without spending hefty sums of money. Adults are always fond of such gadgets and they always welcome and adopt such new technology readily. Further, young people have been able to broaden their minds and improve their skills by doing research on the Internet. For instance, they use smart phones to look up any new word they come across. As we know that most of the universities have online teaching provision and smart phones assist the students to complete their assignments on time.
(3) The mobile phone has been a lifesaver for a lot of people in case of an emergency. Likewise, use of smart phones can be of vital importance in preventing crimes in the society by providing information to the security forces in time.
(4) Nonetheless, for the young the use of mobile phone can be like an addiction and they can misuse it. Young people are also prone to getting involved in undesirable activities on the Internet. This might have adverse effect on their academic performance. Therefore, young people should always be monitored and made aware of its bad outcomes.
(5) Also a major contributor to its popularity is the availability of prepaid or pay as you go services from a phone shop or an online store. This allows subscribers to load text or airtime credits to their handsets by the use of their credit cards, debit cards or by buying a prepaid card from the network they subscribe to. This plan also doesn’t commit a particular customer to a contract. If prepaid card is not that appealing to you, then you can opt to subscribe using the pay by month plan.
In para 1, synonym of ‘innovation’ is ________.
explanation: Paragraph 1 speaks of the innovation of new technologies such as mobile phones and the internet. Innovation means bringing in something new, so its closest synonym is invention.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
1. Children in India live in diverse circumstances and have diverse needs and rights. Along with their need to be educated, healthy and skillful, they need, and have rights to adequate nutrition, to live in a safe and supportive environment, have opportunities to reach their optimal potential and generally lead healthy, joyful and fulfilling lives so that they can be productive and well adjusted citizens of tomorrow.
2. Children in our country face many challenges. Many of them are first generation learners and face myriad problems throughout their schooling. They, due to the socio-economic and cultural determinants may be vulnerable in many ways. Peer pressure and lack of positive role models may prompt them to make unsafe and unhealthy choices. Anxiety and depression amongst the students, to the point of turning them suicidal, have been a cause of concern in the recent past.
3. Girls are more vulnerable and face discrimination at many levels from being unwelcome since birth to being pulled out of school for a variety of reasons. Dropping out of school, low motivation for academics and general disinterest in sports and physical activities too are some of the problems that need to be addressed. Child malnutrition is rampant in most parts of the country. This has an adverse bearing on their cognitive capacities, learning performance and physical capacity.
4. Our children have a right to age appropriate education, skills building, a safe and supportive environment, positive role models, empowerment, and friendly health services and counseling. Well informed and skilled children are likely to make better decisions concerning not only their careers and relationships, habits, physical and mental health, but will be successful and an asset to the society.
5. They also need to understand and deal with emerging issues like newly available career choices, pollution, water and energy conservation, global warming, protection of environment, terrorism and disasters. Dealing with anxiety and depression, negative peer pressure, violence, accidents, are some other significant issues that impact individuals health and also the social, economic and health indicators of the country. Gender sensitivity, prevention of female infanticide and good parenting are some important social issues that all children need to understand. Children require guidance and assistance - both covert and overt- from their Parents, Teachers, peers and society in general to complete the various "tasks" of development and deal with such issues.
Identify the meaning of the word: ‘a great number’ (para 2)
explanation: Paragraph 2 says first generation learners face myriad problems throughout their schooling. Myriad means a countless or very great number of something.

Dropping out of school, low motivation for academics and general disinterest in sports and physical activities too are some of the problems that need to be addressed. Child malnutrition is rampant in most parts of the country. This has an adverse bearing on their cognitive capacities, learning performance and physical capacity.
4. Our children have a right to age appropriate education, skills building, a safe and supportive environment, positive role models, empowerment, and friendly health services and counseling. Well informed and skilled children are likely to make better decisions concerning not only their careers and relationships, habits, physical and mental health, but will be successful and an asset to the society.
5. They also need to understand and deal with emerging issues like newly available career choices, pollution, water and energy conservation, global warming, protection of environment, terrorism and disasters. Dealing with anxiety and depression, negative peer pressure, violence, accidents, are some other significant issues that impact individuals health and also the social, economic and health indicators of the country. Gender sensitivity, prevention of female infanticide and good parenting are some important social issues that all children need to understand. Children require guidance and assistance - both covert and overt- from their Parents, Teachers, peers and society in general to complete the various "tasks" of development and deal with such issues.
Identify a word which means the same as ‘a valuable person or thing’ (para 4)
explanation: Paragraph 4 says well informed children will be successful and an asset to the society. An asset is a useful or valuable person or thing.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
1. Children in India live in diverse circumstances and have diverse needs and rights. Along with their need to be educated, healthy and skillful, they need, and have rights to adequate nutrition, to live in a safe and supportive environment, have opportunities to reach their optimal potential and generally lead healthy, joyful and fulfilling lives so that they can be productive and well adjusted citizens of tomorrow.
2. Children in our country face many challenges. Many of them are first generation learners and face myriad problems throughout their schooling. They, due to the socio-economic and cultural determinants may be vulnerable in many ways. Peer pressure and lack of positive role models may prompt them to make unsafe and unhealthy choices. Anxiety and depression amongst the students, to the point of turning them suicidal, have been a cause of concern in the recent past.
3. Girls are more vulnerable and face discrimination at many levels from being unwelcome since birth to being pulled out of school for a variety of reasons. Dropping out of school, low motivation for academics and general disinterest in sports and physical activities too are some of the problems that need to be addressed. Child malnutrition is rampant in most parts of the country. This has an adverse bearing on their cognitive capacities, learning performance and physical capacity.
4. Our children have a right to age appropriate education, skills building, a safe and supportive environment, positive role models, empowerment, and friendly health services and counseling. Well informed and skilled children are likely to make better decisions concerning not only their careers and relationships, habits, physical and mental health, but will be successful and an asset to the society.
5. They also need to understand and deal with emerging issues like newly available career choices, pollution, water and energy conservation, global warming, protection of environment, terrorism and disasters. Dealing with anxiety and depression, negative peer pressure, violence, accidents, are some other significant issues that impact individuals health and also the social, economic and health indicators of the country. Gender sensitivity, prevention of female infanticide and good parenting are some important social issues that all children need to understand. Children require guidance and assistance - both covert and overt- from their Parents, Teachers, peers and society in general to complete the various "tasks" of development and deal with such issues.
Identify a word which means the opposite of ‘covered’ (para 5)
explanation: Paragraph 5 says children need guidance that is both covert and overt. Covert means hidden or covered, so its opposite overt means open and not covered.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Complete the line from a ‘Save the Environment’ song, by filling the blank with the correct option.
Pollution, pollution, its time to take a stand,
for the health of our planet, we’ve got to lend a hand,
Reduce, reuse, recycle, that’s the key,
________ our world for you and me.
explanation: The line states the purpose of reducing, reusing and recycling. Purpose is expressed with the infinitive, which is to followed by the base form preserve.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Complete the given narrative by filling in the blank with the correct option :
Excited about his newly earned powers, Midas started touching all kinds of things, _____ each item into pure gold.
explanation: The blank begins a participle clause that describes the result of Midas touching things. The present participle turning fits this structure after the comma.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Complete the given narrative by filling in the blank with the correct option :
The school _________, I could not get my certificate.
explanation: The opening phrase gives the reason for not getting the certificate and needs a participle with its own subject. Being closed is the passive present participle that shows the school was shut.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blank by using the correct form of the word in the bracket :
Governments are starting programmes __________ (teach) adults how to read and write.
explanation: The blank expresses the purpose of the programmes. The to-infinitive to teach is used to show purpose after a noun like programmes.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Relative adverb where for a place
question:
Fill in any four of the blanks in the paragraph given below with the help of options that follow :
The modern student ___(a)___ the importance ___(b)___ physical exercise. He spends one to two hours in open air ___(c)___ he takes part in different sports. However, care should ___(d)___ not to overstrain ___(e)___ body.
(c)
explanation: The blank begins a clause that tells us about the place, open air, in which he takes part in sports. The relative adverb where is used to refer to a place, so the sentence reads in open air where he takes part in different sports.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Replace the underlined word used in the sentence with the best option given below : If Hemant take the earlier train, he would not have been late for the meeting.
explanation: The result would not have been late refers to an unreal past situation. Had taken supplies the past perfect condition.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Complete the following sentence by choosing the correct option : If we had consulted the engineer, we _____ this mistake.
explanation: If we had consulted describes an unreal past condition. Would have avoided gives its imagined past result.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Complete the line from a ‘Save the Planet’ song, by filling in the blank with the correct option.
Let’s see what we can do
To save the planet for me and you
E is for environment, keep it clean
If we ___________ together, we’ll make the best team.
explanation: This is a first conditional sentence about a likely future result. The if-clause takes the simple present stand, while the main clause uses will in we will make. The other verb forms do not fit this pattern.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Verb in an if-clause of a reported promise
question: The teacher motivated the students by letting them know that if they _________ submit their assignments by the end of the day, they might get an opportunity to watch the match.
explanation: The official scheme accepts would in the if-clause, expressing the students’ willingness to submit their assignments. Here if they would means if they were willing to, which suits a teacher motivating students.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option.
If I were attending the workshop, I _________ stay on till the end of the second session as well.
explanation: The clause If I were attending shows an imagined, unreal present condition. Such a conditional uses would with the base verb in the main clause.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete the sentence. ______ he ran at breakneck speed he did not manage to catch the bus.
explanation: The sentence contrasts running fast with failing to catch the bus. Although introduces that concession.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Fill in the blank by choosing the right option. ___________ I was not feeling well, I ventured out for a walk.
explanation: Though introduces the contrast between feeling unwell and going for a walk. The other choices do not fit the sentence structure.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Complete the given narrative by filling in the blank with the correct option :
Not only did Mayank work hard to win the trophy, _________ helped the juniors to improve their skills.
explanation: Not only is paired with but also as a correlative conjunction. The second clause therefore begins with but he also.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blanks in the paragraph given below choosing the most appropriate options from the ones that follow.
Baby tigers are ___(a)___ cubs. At eight weeks, the cubs are ready ___(b)___ their mother out of the den. ___(c)___ , they do not travel with her as she roams her territory ___(d)___ they are older.
Blank (c):
explanation: The cubs can leave the den, yet they do not travel with their mother. However is the linker that introduces this contrast at the start of a sentence.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blanks in the paragraph given below choosing the most appropriate options from the ones that follow.
Baby tigers are ___(a)___ cubs. At eight weeks, the cubs are ready ___(b)___ their mother out of the den. ___(c)___ , they do not travel with her as she roams her territory ___(d)___ they are older.
Blank (d):
explanation: The cubs stay back only up to the time they grow older. Till expresses this time limit, giving they do not travel with her till they are older.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Before as a conjunction of time
question:
Read the paragraph given below and fill in the blanks by choosing the most appropriate words from the given options :
A great advantage ___(a)___ early rising is the good start it gives us to our day’s work. An early riser has done a large amount of hard work ___(b)___ other men have got out of their beds. In the early morning, the mind is fresh and there ___(c)___ few noises or other distractions, so that the work done ___(d)___ that time is generally well done.
Choose the correct option for blank (b).
explanation: A conjunction of time is needed to join the two clauses. The early riser finishes much hard work before other men have got out of their beds.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Read the paragraph given below and fill in the blanks by choosing the most appropriate words from the given options.
Buddhism __(a)__ survived in India only __(b)__ a comparatively small section of population __(c)__ Buddhism in __(d)__ Far East today has over 150 million adherents.
Fill in blank (c).
explanation: The two clauses contrast the small following of Buddhism in India with its huge following in the Far East. Though is the conjunction that expresses such a contrast.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Read the paragraph given below and fill in the blanks by choosing the most appropriate words from the given options :
Birds and animals live in the lap ___(a)___ nature and can predict the likely changes accurately. Swallows usually fly high ___(b)___ the sky. But during a storm, they come down ___(c)___ fly close ___(d)___ the ground.
(c)
explanation: The swallows do two things one after the other: they come down and they fly close to the ground. The conjunction and joins two actions that both happen.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Read the paragraph given below and fill in the blanks by choosing the most appropriate words from the given options :
Ram was a child of five, when he ___(a)___ two infants from a burning hut. His elder brother had fought a cheetah ___(b)___ working in the forest. His mother received a bullet ___(c)___ her hand when trying to save her husband from dacoits. This family had ___(d)___ a great courage and presence of mind in moments of crisis.
(b)
explanation: The brother fought the cheetah at the time he was working in the forest. While introduces an ongoing action expressed with an ing form, whereas during must be followed by a noun.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in any four of the following blanks given below choosing the most appropriate options from the ones that follow. Write the answers in your answer sheet against the correct blank numbers.
Communication ___(a)___ become very effective ___(b)___ instant due to smart phones. People are able ___(c)___ convey their messages all around the globe to ___(d)___ loved ones ___(e)___ spending hefty sums of money.
(b)
explanation: The blank joins two qualities of communication, effective and instant. Both describe positive changes brought by smart phones, so the additive conjunction and fits.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Joining two nouns in a compound subject
question:
Complete the paragraph given below by filling in the blanks choosing the correct option from those that follow-
Elephants (a) _____ the largest land mammals. Three species of elephants (b) _____ living today. Elephants (c) ________ other Elephantidae were once classified with other thick skinned. The elephant’s gestation period is 22 months, (d) _________ longest for any land animal.
(c)
explanation: The blank links Elephants and other Elephantidae as a joint subject of the plural verb were. The coordinating conjunction and joins two nouns of equal rank in this way.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blanks choosing the most appropriate option from the ones given in the box.
1. Butterflies are abundant (a) ________ the Central African Republic.
2. It (b) ________ home to nearly 600 identified species.
3. Many butterflies are brilliantly coloured and small (c) ________ some are as big as saucers.
4. Farmer Philippe (d) ________ solace in collecting butterfly wings from his fields and turning them into works of art.
5. My favourite hobby, since my childhood, is (e) ________ butterflies.
(c)
explanation: The sentence contrasts small butterflies with some that are as big as saucers. While is a conjunction that expresses such a contrast between two clauses.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Read the passage given below and fill in the blanks by choosing the most appropriate word from the given options.
It is not possible even for the greatest optimist (a) ________ smile all the time and feel good throughout the day. Every one (b) ________ a tension now or then, when everything seems dark. But once you develop a positive attitude (c) ________ realize that life is a roller coaster ride, a series of ups and downs
(c)
explanation: The blank joins two actions of the same person, developing a positive attitude and realizing that life has ups and downs. The additive conjunction and links these related ideas.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Demonstrative those before a relative clause
question:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete the official notice:
Notification to All Students,
Please note that _________________ applicants who have submitted incomplete forms are required to resubmit their documents by Friday.
explanation: Those is the plural demonstrative used to point out a group that is defined by a following relative clause, as in those applicants who have submitted incomplete forms. This and that are singular and cannot go with the plural noun applicants. These suggests people already near or just mentioned, which does not suit a general notice.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Choose the correct option to fill in the blank.
Saira was disappointed when she saw there was _______ food left to serve the guests.
explanation: Food is an uncountable noun here, so it takes little rather than few. Little means hardly any, which explains why Saira was disappointed. Any is used mainly in negatives and questions, and least is a superlative that does not fit the sentence.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: A school Principal addressed Board aspirants and said : “_______ candidates must carry their identification proof.” Fill in the blank with the appropriate option :
explanation: Candidates is a plural noun in this sentence. All can directly modify that plural noun, while each and every require a singular noun.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blank to complete the sentence in a teacher’s diary by choosing the correct option.
_____ student in the class submitted their assignment on time.
explanation: Every is used with a singular countable noun to refer to each member of a group, so every student in the class is the natural choice. All would need the plural noun students. The phrase in the class and the pronoun their point to a statement about the whole class rather than a single unnamed student.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Choose the correct option to fill the blank.
I looked inside the bucket and saw there was ______ water in it, so they had to add more to use.
explanation: Water is an uncountable noun, so it takes little rather than few. Little means not much, which explains why more water had to be added. Any is used mainly in negatives and questions, and least is a superlative that does not fit here.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Each with a singular countable noun
question:
Fill in the blank choosing the most appropriate option :
The teacher distributed a piece of paper to ________ student.
explanation: The noun student is singular and countable. Each is the determiner used with a singular noun to refer to every member of a group one by one. Few, all and many would need the plural noun students.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blank choosing the most appropriate option :
The news about the retirement of my favourite character gave me _________ disappointment.
explanation: Disappointment is used here as an uncountable noun. Much shows a large amount with uncountable nouns, while many and few go with countable nouns. Little would suggest only a small amount, which does not suit news about a favourite character retiring.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Many with a plural countable noun
question:
Complete the statement made by a career counsellor by filling the blank with the correct option :
In our country, _________ universities offer a range of courses. That’s why foreign students prefer Indian universities.
explanation: Universities is a plural countable noun, so many fits the blank. The second sentence explains that foreign students prefer Indian universities, which points to a large number offering courses. Each needs a singular noun, few gives a negative sense and more needs a comparison.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns
question:
Fill in the blanks by choosing the correct options to conclude the report.
The report concludes that _________ learners have _________ knowledge of astrophysics.
explanation: Learners is a plural countable noun, so very few fits the first blank. Knowledge is an uncountable noun, and some is a suitable quantifier for it. Every cannot be used with a plural noun like learners or with an uncountable noun like knowledge.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill the blank with the correct option to complete the note of appreciation by the Head of an organisation.
It is good to know that ______ registration forms were received this time for our event, as compared to the previous year.
explanation: The phrase as compared to the previous year signals a comparison. More is the comparative determiner used with the plural countable noun registration forms.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Article an before a vowel sound
question:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete the slogan :
_____ EDUCATED MIND CAN TEACH MANY.
explanation: The article an is used before a word beginning with a vowel sound. Educated begins with a vowel sound, so an educated mind is correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blanks for the given line :
Don’t you have _____ friends in the school ?
explanation: Any is used with plural countable nouns in negative sentences and questions. Much and little go with uncountable nouns, and few does not fit a negative question.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blank with the correct option :
The number of people attending this evening’s annual function is _________ than that of the previous year’s.
explanation: The noun number is a single quantity, so it is compared with less rather than fewer. The comparative form is needed because of than, which rules out few and much.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: The little for a small amount
question:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option.
I appreciate even ________ help given to me.
explanation: The little means the small amount that there is, and it is used with uncountable nouns like help. Even the little help shows the speaker values whatever help is given.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete the slogan.
__________ ONLY WEAPON TO FIGHT INJUSTICE IS EDUCATION
explanation: The slogan refers to one particular weapon described as the only one. The definite article the is used before only when a specific and unique thing is meant.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error in a museum plaque and supplies the correction for the same.
These building, inaugurated on 29 March 1954, was a former residence of a Maharaja.
explanation: The noun building and the verb was are singular. The plural demonstrative these must become the singular this.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: There’s never ________ petrol left after Rahul uses the car.
explanation: Petrol is an uncountable noun, so many cannot be used. Much fits naturally with never to show that only a small quantity remains.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Choose the option that completes the paragraph above correctly.
My work requires me to spread awareness about the kinds of bullying prevalent in a student's life. Did you know that one out of __________ five students is bullied by another youth? __________ students are scared of opening up to others about instances of bullying __________ may be happening to or around them.
explanation: One out of every five is the standard expression for a ratio. Many fits because the writer is stressing that a large number of students are scared. That introduces the relative clause describing the instances of bullying.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Singular verb with the article an
question:
Choose the correct options to fill in the blanks to complete the note about the Wangala Festival of Meghalaya.
The Wangala -(i)- festival for the Garo in Meghalaya, Assam and Nagaland. It is a post-harvest festival -(ii)- the end of the agricultural year. It is popularly known as ‘The Hundred Drums’ festival. During the signature dance, the leading warrior -(iii)- with synchronised dance steps and specific hand-head movements.
Blank (i):
explanation: The singular subject The Wangala takes the singular verb is, and the note describes a present fact. The countable noun festival needs an article, and an is used before the vowel sound of important.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blanks by choosing the correct options for ANY FOUR of the six sentences given below.
The good news is that…………… volunteers dropped out this month than the last two.
explanation: Volunteers is a plural countable noun, so fewer is used rather than less. The comparison with than also requires the comparative form fewer.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Articles a and an by sound
question:
Fill in the blanks by choosing the correct options for ANY FOUR of the six sentences given below.
It was …………… historic day for the organisation when …………….. honour was bestowed upon its employees.
explanation: Historic begins with a pronounced h sound, which is a consonant sound, so a is used. Honour begins with a silent h and a vowel sound, so an is used.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Indefinite article before a consonant sound
question:
Fill in the blanks in the paragraph given below by choosing the most appropriate options from the ones that follow. Write the answers in your answer sheet against the correct blank numbers.
Reading books ___(a)___ a good hobby. Books open ___(b)___ vast new world to us. They increase ___(c)___ knowledge and change our outlook ___(d)___ the world.
(b)
explanation: The phrase vast new world refers to a world not mentioned before, so an indefinite article is needed. Vast begins with a consonant sound, so a is used rather than an.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blanks in the paragraph given below by choosing the most appropriate options from the ones that follow. Write the answers in your answer sheet against the correct blank numbers.
Reading books ___(a)___ a good hobby. Books open ___(b)___ vast new world to us. They increase ___(c)___ knowledge and change our outlook ___(d)___ the world.
(c)
explanation: The paragraph speaks of books opening a world to us. The same sentence continues with change our outlook, so the possessive determiner our keeps the reference consistent.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in the blanks to complete the paragraph given below with the help of options that follow :
You play to win but a good sportsperson ___(a)___ that defeat may also come once in a while. There are times when others ___(b)___ do better than you. What you should look to do is to maximize your chances of success. And ___(c)___ only way you ___(d)___ do this is by being yourself.
Choose the correct option for blank (c).
explanation: The definite article is used before only when it points to one particular thing. The phrase the only way refers to a single specific way.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Definite article with the Far East
question:
Read the paragraph given below and fill in the blanks by choosing the most appropriate words from the given options.
Buddhism __(a)__ survived in India only __(b)__ a comparatively small section of population __(c)__ Buddhism in __(d)__ Far East today has over 150 million adherents.
Fill in blank (d).
explanation: The Far East is the name of a particular geographical region and takes the definite article. So the phrase is Buddhism in the Far East.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Base verb and any in a question with did
question:
Complete the dialogue given below with the help of options that follow :
Ramita : When did you arrive in Mumbai, Mr. Rohit ?
Rohit : I ___(a)___ yesterday.
Ramita : Did you ___(b)___ on the way ?
Rohit : Yes, someone ___(c)___ my bag while I was sleeping in the train.
Ramita : It is a very sad news. What important things ___(d)___ ?
Rohit : My passport, business documents and many other important things.
(b)
explanation: The auxiliary did is followed by the base form of the verb, so have is needed and not had. In questions, any is normally used before a noun like difficulty, which gives have any difficulty.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Fill in any four of the following blanks given below choosing the most appropriate options from the ones that follow. Write the answers in your answer sheet against the correct blank numbers.
Communication ___(a)___ become very effective ___(b)___ instant due to smart phones. People are able ___(c)___ convey their messages all around the globe to ___(d)___ loved ones ___(e)___ spending hefty sums of money.
(d)
explanation: The loved ones belong to the people mentioned at the start of the sentence. People is plural, so the possessive determiner their is needed.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Definite article before a known noun
question:
Fill in any four of the blanks in the paragraph given below with the help of options that follow :
The modern student ___(a)___ the importance ___(b)___ physical exercise. He spends one to two hours in open air ___(c)___ he takes part in different sports. However, care should ___(d)___ not to overstrain ___(e)___ body.
(e)
explanation: The body meant here is the student’s own body, which is already clear from the context. The definite article the is used before such a specific noun, so the phrase is overstrain the body.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Which for a choice from a limited set
question:
The given question has an error. Select the option that correctly identifies the error and the correction.
What among these books have you read before?
explanation: The question asks about a choice from a specific, limited group of books, which calls for which rather than what. Among is correct for more than two books, and these and have already agree with books and with you.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line taken from an aircraft’s safety manual. Demonstrate use of seat belts and ensuring that all passengers have their seat belts fastened before take-off and landing.
explanation: The sentence gives parallel instructions joined by and. Ensure matches the imperative verb demonstrate.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the line given below : I don’t know what it is. It feel like an incredibly lucky day for me. Option No. Error Correction
explanation: The pronoun it takes the singular verb feels in the present tense. Feel is the incorrect form in the sentence.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the line given below : Mohini attend every concert in the city because she loves classical music. Option No. Error Correction
explanation: Mohini is a singular subject in the present tense. Attend therefore changes to attends.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Identify and correct the error in the given line. I prefer the chocolate pudding than the vanilla truffle anyday. Option No. Error Correction
explanation: The standard construction is prefer one thing to another. Replacing than with to corrects the comparison.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the given sentence. Neither of the options are suitable for our needs at the present moment. Option No. Error Correction
explanation: Neither functions as a singular subject here. Are should therefore change to is.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Identify and correct the error in the given line taken from a critical review of a recently staged play : ‘As an actor, Ravi Raj, is superior then any other contemporary actor.’ Options Error Correction
explanation: Superior is followed by to in a comparison. Changing then to to corrects the printed line.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The given question has an error. Select the option that correctly identifies the error and the correction.
Which kind of person does something like that?
explanation: An open, general question about the type or nature of a person uses what kind of rather than which kind of. Which is used for a choice from a limited, known set, and no such set is given here. The words kind, something and that are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: Select the option that identifies the error and provides the correction. The complicated story line of the novel kept me engross. Option No. Error Correction
explanation: Kept me requires an adjective or participial complement. Engrossed describes the readers absorbed state.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line taken from an article about growing obesity.
Obesity in teenage children is a major concern between parents today.
explanation: Between is used when referring to two people or things. Parents here refers to a larger group, so the preposition among is required.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the opening line, from an analytical paragraph.
The advent of social media has revolutionized communication by connected people across the globe in unprecedented ways.
explanation: A preposition such as by must be followed by a gerund, so connected should be connecting. The singular subject advent correctly takes has, and the other words are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Identify and correct the error in the given line taken from a user manual of an ironing board.
Place the garment on the ironing board, smoothening out as many wrinkle as possible.
explanation: Many is used with plural countable nouns. The phrase as many wrinkle therefore needs the plural form wrinkles. The other words in the line are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Tense consistency in a habitual action
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the line given below :
He usually ate breakfast before he goes to school.
explanation: The adverb usually and the present tense verb goes show that the line describes a daily habit. Habits are expressed in the simple present tense, so ate must change to eats. The official scheme marks ate as the error and eats as the correction.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Simple past with In earlier times
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the line given below :
In earlier times, public libraries plays an important role in the lives of the people.
explanation: The phrase In earlier times places the action in the past. The present tense verb plays must therefore change to the simple past played, which also suits the plural subject libraries.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The following is an excerpt from a travelogue :
There is an error in the statement. Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction.
Kanyakumari is popular for its beautiful beaches, unique Vivekananda Rock Memorial and stunning sunrise and sunset view.
explanation: The noun view refers to both the sunrise and the sunset, which are two separate sights. It must therefore take the plural form views. The subject Kanyakumari is singular, so is and the phrase popular for are correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Nearly every with a singular noun
question:
Identify and correct the error in the given line taken from an online news report:
Nearly most shop was closed for the public holiday.
explanation: Nearly cannot sensibly modify most, and most would also need a plural noun. Nearly every is the correct expression, and every takes a singular noun and verb. The corrected line reads that nearly every shop was closed for the public holiday.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for a pop-up that appeared on a webpage.
These cookies are used to collect information about how you interact with our website and allows us to remember you.
explanation: The subject of allows is cookies, which is plural. A plural subject takes the plural verb allow, matching are used earlier in the sentence.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Conjunction and in place of or
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for a privacy policy document.
We process this data to supply the goods as well as services you have purchased or to keep records of such transactions.
explanation: The sentence gives two purposes for processing the data, supplying the goods and keeping records. Both purposes apply together, so the conjunction and is needed instead of or.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for a website’s terms and conditions document.
We reserve the right to make change to this website at any time without notice and it is your responsibility to revisit this page from time to time to re-read these terms.
explanation: Change in this sense is a countable noun, so it cannot stand alone without an article or a plural ending. The usual expression is to make changes to something.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the opening line, from a Terms and Conditions document.
Though all efforts have been made to ensure the accuracy of the content on this website, the same could not be construed as a statement of law or used for any legal purposes.
explanation: The sentence is a disclaimer telling readers how the content ought not to be used. The modal should expresses this advice or obligation, while could only suggests possibility. The other words in the sentence are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Modal will in a policy statement
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the opening line of a Privacy Policy document.
Your email address can only be recorded if you choose to send a message. It will not be used for any other purpose, and will not be disclosed without your consent.
explanation: The policy states what will definitely happen to an email address, matching the later clauses with will not be used and will not be disclosed. So can is replaced by will for consistency and certainty. The verb choose already agrees with you, and purpose and for are correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the opening line of a Policy document.
Material featured on this website should be reproduced free of charge. However, the material has to be reproduced accurately and is not to be used in a derogatory or in a misleading context.
explanation: The policy is giving permission to reproduce material free of charge. The modal may expresses permission, while should wrongly suggests an obligation. The words however, has and material are already used correctly.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction in the given sentence :
Air pollution is continuous damaging the whole ecological system affecting the lives of plants and animals as well.
explanation: The word continuous is an adjective, but here it modifies the verb phrase is damaging. A verb must be modified by an adverb, so continuous should be replaced with continuously.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Using the noun youth after the
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the sentence from a public health campaign.
The campaign’s goal is to increase physical activity among the younger.
explanation: After the article the, the sentence needs a noun naming a group of people. Younger is a comparative adjective and cannot stand alone here, so it is replaced by the noun youth. The other words are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Base form of the verb after to
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction in the given sentence :
She wants to learns how to play the piano.
explanation: The verb that follows to in an infinitive must be in its base form. Learns has a third person ending, so it is corrected to learn. Wants and play are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Base form of the verb after encourage someone to
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction in the given sentence from a public health campaign :
The campaign encourages parents to reducing screen time for their children.
explanation: The verb encourage follows the pattern encourage someone to do something. The infinitive needs the base form, so reducing is corrected to reduce. Encourages agrees with the singular subject campaign.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction from a scientific review.
The study examines the association among exposure to sunlight and vitamin D levels in the body.
explanation: The sentence links exactly two things, exposure to sunlight and vitamin D levels. Between is used for two items, while among is used for three or more. The singular verb examines correctly agrees with the study.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Subject-verb agreement with a singular subject
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction.
My pet dog are very playful
explanation: The subject my pet dog is singular. A singular subject takes the singular verb is, not the plural are. The words My, pet and playful are already correct in the sentence.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Base form of the verb after to
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the public health campaign.
Our goal is to promoting healthier meal choices in schools and at home.
explanation: The infinitive marker to is followed by the base form of the verb. So is to promoting must become is to promote. The words goal, choices and in are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for a line from a Research Report :
In many low and middle income countries, health coverage has improved dramatically in the last two decades, but health outcomes may not.
explanation: The clause but health outcomes may not stands for an unstated verb that must match has improved. Replacing may with have gives but health outcomes have not, which completes the present perfect contrast.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for a line from a Research Report :
The search for better employment opportunities are the key mechanism by which the majority of the world’s population can hope to improve their lives.
explanation: The subject of the sentence is the singular noun search, not opportunities. A singular subject needs is, so are must be corrected to is.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Past participle in an elliptical if clause
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for a line from a Research Report on Water Conservation.
Excess pumping of groundwater leads to decrease in groundwater levels but if continues, it can exhaust the resource.
explanation: The clause if continues has no subject, and it refers to the pumping being continued. The past participle gives the correct shortened form if continued, meaning if it is continued.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the closing line, from an analytical report.
In conclusion, this study explores the association among short-sleep pattern and overweight youngsters.
explanation: Among is used for more than two people or things, while between links two items. The sentence relates exactly two things, a short-sleep pattern and overweight youngsters. So among must be replaced by between.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Past form of the modal can
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line :
I can run fast when I was young.
explanation: The clause when I was young places the ability in the past. The past form of the modal can is could, so the sentence should read I could run fast when I was young.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line from the health report :
The incidence of malaria have reduced in the city.
explanation: The subject of the sentence is the singular noun incidence, not malaria. A singular subject needs has, so have reduced should be has reduced.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line from a news report. :
The traffic situation in the city calls out immediate intervention by the traffic police.
explanation: To call for something means to require or demand it. The situation requires intervention, so calls out should be calls for.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following sentence :
Twenty years ago, kids at school had never even heard of the internet.
explanation: The official scheme marks at as the error and in as the correction, giving kids in school. The other changes would make the sentence wrong, for example twenty year ago or have heard in a past time frame.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line from a sports journal :
The captain of the team was accused with not encouraging the team members.
explanation: The verb accuse is followed by the preposition of, not with. The corrected sentence reads accused of not encouraging the team members.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line :
The children cheers loudly when their captain scored the winning goal.
explanation: The verb scored shows that the action took place in the past. So cheers must change to the past form cheered to keep the tenses consistent.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line :
Nearly all the sports practised nowadays is competitive.
explanation: The subject of the verb is all the sports, which is plural. A plural subject takes the plural verb are, so is must be replaced by are.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Preposition in peace in the world
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line :
World leaders should work to establish peace of the world so that human and economic resources could be used to meet the pressing demands of mankind.
explanation: The correct expression is peace in the world, so the preposition of must be replaced by in. The conjunction so that and the verbs could and meet are used correctly.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line from a news report :
The winning athletes were felicitation by the State Government and the City Council.
explanation: The sentence is in the passive voice, which needs were followed by a past participle. The noun felicitation must therefore be replaced by the past participle felicitated.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line from a news report :
Yesterday, two man were rescued from a deep sewer by a policeman.
explanation: The number two requires a plural noun, so man must become men. The plural verb were also agrees with men. The passive form were rescued and the prepositions from and by are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line :
At the end of the street stand the tallest building in the city.
explanation: In this inverted sentence the subject comes after the verb. The subject the tallest building is singular, so the verb must be stands. The other words are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line from a magazine article :
Blogging today is increasingly gaining on popularity.
explanation: The correct expression is to gain in popularity, meaning to become more popular. Gaining on means catching up with someone, so on must be replaced by in. The other words are already correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Tense consistency in a general rule
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following traffic advisory :
Whoever drove a motor vehicle without a safety belt or carries passengers without seat belts will be fined.
explanation: A traffic advisory states a general rule, so it uses the simple present tense. Drove must change to drives to match carries in the same clause.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line :
My sister lives at the ground floor of a two-storeyed apartment and hates living there.
explanation: A person lives on a particular floor of a building, not at it. The preposition at must therefore be replaced by on.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line :
I can’t never forget my childhood friend Bella.
explanation: The sentence has a double negative because both can’t and never are negative. Replacing can’t with can leaves the single negative never and makes the sentence correct.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following sentence :
More of the fun and excitement in our lives comes from using our imagination.
explanation: The sentence refers to the greater part of the fun and excitement in our lives. Most is the determiner that expresses the largest part of a whole, so More must be changed to Most.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line :
The sounds of laughter was echoing in the corridor.
explanation: The verb was is singular, so the subject it refers to must also be singular. Changing sounds to sound gives The sound of laughter was echoing in the corridor.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line :
Rahul along with his cousins are leaving for sea.
explanation: When a subject is joined to another noun by along with, the verb agrees with the first subject. Rahul is singular, so are must be changed to is.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Article error in a news report
question:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the following line, from a news report:
Last week a child was not allowed to board the plane at Ranchi airport.
explanation: The plane is mentioned for the first time in the report and is not identified earlier. The official scheme corrects the definite article the to the indefinite article a.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Format elements of a letter to the editor
question:
You are Debashree, a resident of Siliguri, Assam. You have to write a letter to the editor of a national daily drawing attention towards the difficulty faced by differently-abled people at tourist places.
Select the option with relevant aspects that Debashree should select, for this letter.
(1) The newspaper’s name
(2) Attached proof of the newspaper subscription
(3) Debashree’s address
(4) Formal tone
(5) Expected date of the letter’s receipt
explanation: A letter to the editor carries the sender’s address and the name of the newspaper in the receiver’s address. It must also be written in a formal tone. Proof of subscription and the expected date of receipt are not part of the format.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Subject line of a letter to the editor
question:
You are Debashree, a resident of Siliguri, Assam. You have to write a letter to the editor of a national daily drawing attention towards the difficulty faced by differently-abled people at tourist places.
Select the appropriate subject for this letter.
options: (C) Tourist places are an inconvenience to differently-abled people
(D) Inconvenience Faced by the Differently-abled at Tourist Spots
answer: (D) Inconvenience Faced by the Differently-abled at Tourist Spots
explanation: A subject line should state the exact issue briefly and formally. The chosen subject names both the problem faced and the place, tourist spots, while the others are vague, sound like an article title or overgeneralise.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
You are Debashree, a resident of Siliguri, Assam. You have to write a letter to the editor of a national daily drawing attention towards the difficulty faced by differently-abled people at tourist places.
Which option should Debashree select, to elaborate on the difficulties faced by the differently-abled?
options: (A) Absence of ramps for wheelchairs; Unclean toilets; High ticket-prices
(B) Unsuitable visiting timings; Tourist guides untrained in sign language; Lack of braille-script tourist pamphlets
(C) Absence of ramps for wheelchairs; Tourist guides untrained in sign language; Lack of braille-script tourist pamphlets
(D) Unclean toilets; High ticket-prices; Unsuitable visiting timings
answer: (C) Absence of ramps for wheelchairs; Tourist guides untrained in sign language; Lack of braille-script tourist pamphlets
explanation: Missing wheelchair ramps, guides untrained in sign language and the lack of braille pamphlets affect differently-abled visitors in particular. Unclean toilets, high ticket prices and unsuitable timings trouble all tourists alike.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
You are Debashree, a resident of Siliguri, Assam. You have to write a letter to the editor of a national daily drawing attention towards the difficulty faced by differently-abled people at tourist places.
Debashree shares some suggestions in her letter, to address the issue.
Select the option that helps her complete these suggestions, appropriately.
In my opinion, the media can play a pivotal role in transforming people’s (i)__________. Also, (ii)__________ against negligence to the needs of the differently-abled, at the tourist spots, shall go a long way in bringing about a positive change.
options: (B) (i) perceptions and attitudes (ii) cautioning the authorities
answer: (B) (i) perceptions and attitudes (ii) cautioning the authorities
explanation: The media can change how people view the differently-abled, which is a matter of perceptions and attitudes. Cautioning the authorities is a constructive, formal step against negligence at tourist spots.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
You are Debashree, a resident of Siliguri, Assam. You have to write a letter to the editor of a national daily drawing attention towards the difficulty faced by differently-abled people at tourist places.
Select the option that correctly justifies the choice of the concluding portion of this letter.
(1) I expect the authorities to take actions on this issue. Please post my thoughts in your newspaper.
(2) I hope my views get published in the columns of your newspaper so that this issue may garner more public support and awareness.
options: (A) Yes, to Option (1) because of the authoritative tone.
(B) No, to Option (1) because of the informal tone.
(C) Yes, to Option (2) because of the tone of polite expectation.
(D) No, to Option (2) because of the certainty in the tone.
answer: (C) Yes, to Option (2) because of the tone of polite expectation.
explanation: A letter to the editor should close with a polite request for publication. The second conclusion expresses hope politely and states the purpose of spreading awareness, while the first sounds demanding.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
You are Debashree, a resident of Siliguri, Assam. You have to write a letter to the editor of a national daily drawing attention towards the difficulty faced by differently-abled people at tourist places.
Select the option that completes the concluding line appropriately.
I hope that my letter will ………………
options: (A) help spread awareness about the issue.
(B) lead to action against all authorities responsible, at tourist spots.
(C) improve circulation of the national daily.
(D) result in positive reviews by the readers.
answer: (A) help spread awareness about the issue.
explanation: The aim of a letter to the editor is to bring a public issue to the notice of readers and officials. Hoping it will spread awareness about the issue is the most suitable close.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Essential elements of a letter to the editor
question:
You are Sneha, a resident of Hubli, Karnataka. You have to write a letter to the editor of a national daily, drawing attention to families who are paying their domestic workers below Karnataka's minimum wage of Rs. 195 for eight hours of work per day.
Which of these elements are most important for Sneha to include in the given letter?
(I) a formal tone
(II) creative graphics and images
(III) the sender's and receiver's address
(IV) a narrative of one's own experience
explanation: A letter to the editor is a formal letter, so it needs a formal tone. It must also carry the addresses of the sender and the receiver. Graphics and a personal narrative are not essential parts of such a letter.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
You are Sneha, a resident of Hubli, Karnataka. You have to write a letter to the editor of a national daily, drawing attention to families who are paying their domestic workers below Karnataka's minimum wage of Rs. 195 for eight hours of work per day.
Which subject line should Sneha select for the given letter?
options: (A) The Problem of Unaffordable Domestic Services
(B) The Problem of Illegally Underpaid Domestic Workers
(C) The Issues with Poor Domestic Services in Karnataka
(D) The Issues with the Regularity of Payment to Workers
answer: (B) The Problem of Illegally Underpaid Domestic Workers
explanation: The issue is that families pay domestic workers less than the legal minimum wage. This subject line names that exact problem of illegal underpayment. The other subject lines talk about services or regularity of payment, which is not the concern.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Describing the problem in the introduction
question:
You are Sneha, a resident of Hubli, Karnataka. You have to write a letter to the editor of a national daily, drawing attention to families who are paying their domestic workers below Karnataka's minimum wage of Rs. 195 for eight hours of work per day.
Which of these should Sneha include while DESCRIBING the PROBLEM in the introduction of her letter?
options:
(A) ♦ Citizens should be made aware of the Proper wages.
♦ Domestic workers should demand more fair wages.
♦ The government should check the wages paid to workers and solve this issue.

(B) ♦ Different households have been paying these amounts to the workers.
♦ The workers are not able to make ends meet with such low wages.
♦ The Minimum Wages Act lays down certain rights that should be met.

(C) ♦ The history of wages for domestic workers is very interesting.
♦ Minimum wages were set to help workers afford basic amenities.
♦ Certain issues like working hours and are not addressed by minimum wages.

(D) ♦ Minimum wages should be changed to improve living conditions for domestic workers.
