subject: English Language & Literature
topic: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
question: Mandela refers to liberty as “newborn” because it
options: (A) was dependent on others for growth and guidance.
(B) had recently been attained with lots of struggle.
answer: (B) had recently been attained with lots of struggle.
explanation: South Africa had only just gained freedom from apartheid after a long struggle. Calling the liberty newborn shows that it had recently come into being.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
subtopic: Line hinting at the end of apartheid
question: Which of these lines from 'A Long Walk to Freedom' hints at the end of apartheid in South Africa?
options: (A) I was not born with a hunger to be free. I was born free — free in every way that I could know.
(B) ...I yearned for the basic and honourable freedoms of achieving my potential, of earning my keep,...
(C) Although that day neither group knew the lyrics of the anthem they once despised, they would soon know the words by heart.
(D) ...the white-skinned peoples of South Africa patched up their differences and erected a system of racial domination against the dark-skinned peoples...
answer: (C) Although that day neither group knew the lyrics of the anthem they once despised, they would soon know the words by heart.
explanation: At the inauguration, whites and blacks sang each other's anthems, which they had once despised. Mandela says they would soon know the words by heart, which points to unity between the races. This hints at the end of apartheid.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
He just felt a bit dizzy Then he flapped his wings once and he soared upwards. “Ga, ga, ga, Ga, ga, ga, Gaw-col-ah,” his mother swooped past him, her wings making a loud noise. He answered her with another scream. Then his father flew over him screaming. He saw his two brothers and his sister flying around him curvetting and banking and soaring and diving. Then he completely forgot that he had not always been able to fly, and commended himself to dive and soar and curve, shrieking shrilly.
Read the following sound and movement words.
i) flapped
ii) shrieking
iii) swooped
iv) soared
v) screaming
Select the option that correctly categorises (i) –(v) into sound and movement words.
options: (A) Sound: i, ii, v; Movement: iii, iv
(B) Sound: iv, v; Movement: i, ii, iii
(C) Sound: ii, v; Movement: i, iii, iv
(D) Sound: v; Movement: i, ii, iii, iv
answer: (C) Sound: ii, v; Movement: i, iii, iv
explanation: Shrieking and screaming describe noises the seagulls make, so they are sound words. Flapped, swooped and soared describe actions of the wings and body in flight, so they are movement words. Only one grouping places ii and v under sound and i, iii and iv under movement.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
He felt certain that his wings would never support him; so he bent his head and ran away back to the little hole under the ledge where he slept at night. Even when each of his brothers and his little sister, whose wings were far shorter than his own, ran to the brink, flapped their wings, and flew away, he failed to muster up courage to take that plunge which appeared to him so desperate. His father and mother had come around calling to him shrilly, upbraiding him, threatening to let him starve on his ledge unless he flew away. But for the life of him he could not move.
Which phrase or word would correctly substitute ‘muster up’ in the given sentence from the extract ?
He failed to ‘muster up’ courage to take that plunge which appeared to him so desperate.
explanation: To muster up courage means to gather or summon it. The young seagull could not collect enough courage to take the plunge from the ledge.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The moon was coming up in the east, behind me, and stars were shining in the clear sky above me. There wasn’t a cloud in the sky. I was happy to be alone high up above the sleeping countryside. I was flying my old Dakota aeroplane over France back to England. I was dreaming of my holiday and looking forward to being with my family. I looked at my watch: one thirty in the morning.
What time of the day is the above extract set in ?
explanation: The narrator sees the moon coming up and stars shining in the clear sky. He checks his watch and finds it is one thirty in the morning. Both details show that the extract is set at night.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
That was twenty-four hours ago. Since then nobody had come near him. The day before, all day long, he had watched his parents flying about with his brothers and sister, perfecting them in the art of flight, teaching them how to skim the waves and how to dive for fish. He had, in fact, seen his elder brother catch his first herring and devour it, standing on a rock, while his parents circled around raising a proud cackle and all the morning the whole family had walked about on the big plateau midway down the opposite cliff taunting him for his cowardice.
The word ‘devour’ in the above extract most nearly means
explanation: To devour means to eat something hungrily and quickly. The elder brother catches his first herring and devours it, which means he gobbled it up.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Effect of the first plunge on the young seagull
question:
With a loud scream he fell outwards and downwards into space. Then a monstrous terror seized him and his heart stood still. He could hear nothing. But it only lasted a minute. The next moment he felt his wings spread outwards. The wind rushed against his breast feathers, then under his stomach, and against his wings. He could feel the tips of his wings cutting through the air. He was not falling headlong now. He was soaring gradually downwards and outwards.
What effect does the experience, as described in the lines below, have on the baby seagull?
With a loud scream he fell outwards and downwards into space. Then a monstrous terror seized him and his heart stood still.
Chose the most suitable option.
explanation: The young seagull screams, a monstrous terror seizes him and his heart stands still. These details show that the experience overwhelms him with fear. He feels the thrill of flying only later, when his wings spread outwards.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Pilot unable to see inside the clouds
question:
Inside the clouds, everything was suddenly black. It was impossible to see anything outside the aeroplane. The old aeroplane jumped and twisted in the air. I looked at the compass. I couldn’t believe my eyes the compass was turning round and round and round. It was dead. It would not work. The other instruments were suddenly dead, too. I tried the radio. “Paris Control? Paris Control ? Can you hear me?” There was no answer. The radio was dead too. I had no radio, no compass, and I could not see where I was. I was lost in the storm.
As soon as the pilot was inside the cloud __________
options: (D) he was jumping up and down.
explanation: The extract says that inside the clouds everything was suddenly black and it was impossible to see anything outside the aeroplane. This means the pilot could not see, so his vision was obstructed.

options: (B) Ragini twisted the story to suit the occasion.

answer: (D) Ragini matched the swimmer as he twisted twice in the air before diving into the water.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: The purpose of the treatment, given to the young seagull by his parents, was to…………..
options: (A) teach him a lesson about the importance of food.
(D) improve his relationship with his siblings.
explanation: The young seagull was afraid to fly while his siblings had already flown. His parents left him alone and hungry so that he would overcome his fear and take his first flight.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
In the line given below from 'Black Aeroplane', when the writer refers to the clouds as black mountains, what is he referring to?
They looked like black mountains standing in front of me across the sky.
options: (A) his hopelessness due to imminent death
(B) his despair for having to take a detour
(C) his excitement to fly over them
(D) his fear of their enormous size
answer: (D) his fear of their enormous size
explanation: The pilot compares the storm clouds to black mountains standing across the sky in front of him. The image shows how huge and threatening the clouds looked. It reflects his fear of their enormous size.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Change in the seagull's attitude to flying
question: How does the young seagull's attitude towards flying CHANGE in the story 'The First Flight'?
options: (A) He questions it and then accepts it.
(B) He enjoys it and then finds it uninteresting.
(C) He is uncertain about it and then finds it thrilling.
(D) He is curious about it and then thinks it is overrated.
answer: (C) He is uncertain about it and then finds it thrilling.
explanation: At first the young seagull is afraid and unsure that his wings will support him. Once he begins to fly, he is thrilled and screams with joy. His attitude changes from uncertainty to excitement.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: From the Diary of Anne Frank
question:
“Paper has more patience than people. I thought of this saying on one of those days when I was feeling a little depressed and was sitting at home with my chin in my hands, bored and listless, wondering whether to stay in or go out. I finally stayed where I was, brooding : Yes, paper does have more patience, and since I’m not planning to let anyone else read this stiff backed notebook grandly referred to as a ‘diary’, unless I should ever find a real friend, it probably won’t make a bit of difference.”
The narrator enhances the narrative technique of the extract by using :
explanation: Anne describes herself sitting with her chin in her hands, brooding over the saying that paper has more patience than people. She turns inward to examine her own mood and her reason for keeping a diary. This thoughtful, inward-looking style makes the narration reflective.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: From the Diary of Anne Frank
question:
Writing in a diary is a really strange experience for someone like me. Not only because I’ve never written anything before, but also because it seems to me that later on neither I nor anyone else will be interested in the musings of a thirteen-year-old schoolgirl. Oh well, it doesn’t matter. I feel like writing, and I have an even greater need to get all kinds of things off my chest.
‘Paper has more patience than people.’ I thought of this saying on one of those days when I was feeling a little depressed and was sitting at home with my chin in my hands, bored and listless, wondering whether to stay in or go out. I finally stayed where I was, brooding : Yes, paper does have more patience and since I’m not planning to let anyone else read this stiff-backed notebook grandly referred to as a ‘diary’ unless I should ever find a real friend, it probably won’t make a bit of difference.
What word best describes Anne ?
explanation: Anne thinks carefully about why writing a diary feels strange and why she still wants to write. She broods over the saying that paper has more patience than people, which shows a reflective nature.

explanation: After a day of aloofness, Mijbil came to the bed as he began to settle down and grow friendly. The extract says he remained asleep in the crook of Maxwell’s knees till morning. Nothing suggests that he came to play, so this is not a reason.

question: It was a new bus, its outside painted a gleaming white with some green stripes along the sides. Inside, the overhead bars shone like silver. Directly in front of Valli, above the windshield, there was a beautiful clock. The seats were soft and luxurious. Valli devoured everything with her eyes. But when she started to look outside, she found her view cut off by a canvas blind that covered the lower part of her window. So she stood up on the seat and peered over the blind. (Madam Rides a Bus) The effect on Valli as she describes the bus reveals that she is _________. Choose the most suitable option.
explanation: Valli notices and admires every detail of the new bus. Her fascination shows that she is awed by it.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Why Valli refused to see the sights
question:
“Don't you want to have a look a the sights, now that you’re here ?”
“All by myself ? Oh, I'd be much too afraid.”
Greatly amused by the girl’s way of speaking, the conductor said, “But you weren’t afraid to come in the bus.”
“Nothing to be afraid about that,” she answered.
Why did the girl not want to look at the sights ?
options: (C) She did not want to go with the conductor.
explanation: Valli replies that she would be much too afraid to see the sights all by herself. Her fear of going alone is the reason she refuses.

question:

“Nothing to be afraid about that,” she answered.
Select the option that correctly captures the application of the word ‘sight’ as used in the extract.
options: (A) Rashid could not sight the tiger.
(B) Rashi lost his sight in the left eye.
(C) The General ordered the soldiers not to shoot at sight when they saw the enemy.
(D) Rashid was fascinated by the sights of the city as he went on a tour.
answer: (D) Rashid was fascinated by the sights of the city as he went on a tour.
explanation: In the extract, sights means the interesting places worth seeing in the town. Rashid being fascinated by the sights of the city uses the word in the same sense. The other sentences use sight to mean seeing, eyesight or being seen.

The last line indicates the girl’s
explanation: In the last line Valli says there was nothing to be afraid about in coming on the bus. This shows her self-confidence in travelling alone.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Valli’s reaction to the elderly man
question:
Suddenly she was startled by a voice. “Listen, child,” said the voice, “you shouldn’t stand like that. Sit down.”
Sitting down, she looked to see who had spoken. It was an elderly man who had honestly been concerned for her, but she was annoyed by his attention.
“There’s nobody here who’s a child,” she said haughtily. “I’ve paid my thirty paise like everyone else.”
The conductor chimed in. “Oh, sir, but this is a very grown-up madam. Do you think a mere girl could pay her own fare and travel to the city all alone?”
Valli shot an angry glance at the conductor and said, “I am not a madam. Please remember that. And you’ve not yet given me my ticket.”
“I’ll remember,” the conductor said, mimicking her tone. Everyone laughed, and gradually Valli too joined in the laughter.
How did Valli feel when the elderly man expressed concern that she was standing?
explanation: The extract says Valli was annoyed by the elderly man’s attention. Being annoyed means she was displeased with his concern.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Natalya: But what’s this? Why, you’re in evening dress! Well, I never! Are you going to a ball or what? Though I must say you look better…Tell me, why are you got up like that?
Lomov: [excited] You see, honoured Natalya Stepanova…the fact is, I’ve made up my mind to ask you to hear me out…Of course you’ll be surprised and perhaps even angry, but a…[aside] It’s awfully cold!
Natalya: What’s the matter? [pause] Well?
Lomov: I shall try to be brief: You must know, honoured Natalya Stepanova, that I have long, since my childhood, in fact, had the privilege of knowing your family. My late aunt and her husband, from whom, as you know, I inherited my land, always had the greatest respect for your father and your late mother.
What do the ellipses (…) in Lomov’s speech highlight?
options: (A) reveals his struggle to articulate his prepared thoughts
(B) shows his overconfidence and casual attitude
(C) demonstrates his anxiety and emotional turmoil
(D) indicates a lack of intelligence and education
answer: (C) demonstrates his anxiety and emotional turmoil
explanation: Lomov keeps breaking off in mid-sentence while trying to make his proposal. These pauses, together with the stage direction excited and his aside that it is awfully cold, show his nervousness and inner agitation. Nothing in the extract suggests overconfidence or a lack of education.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Lomov : Hear me out, I implore you ! The peasants of your father’s grandfather, as I have already had the honour of explaining to you, used to bake bricks for my aunt’s grandmother. Now my aunt’s grandmother, wishing to make them a present.
Natalya : I can’t make head or tail of all this about aunts and grandfathers and grandmothers. The Meadows are ours, that’s all.
Lomov : Mine
Natalya : Ours ! You can go proving it for two days on end.
What is Lomov pleading for ?
options: (D) for two days time to prove himself
explanation: Lomov begins with Hear me out, I implore you, which is an earnest request to be listened to. He is pleading with Natalya to hear his explanation about the Meadows.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
LOMOV: It's cold... I'm trembling all over, just as if I’d got an examination before me. The great thing is, I must have my mind made up. If I give myself time to think, to hesitate, to talk a lot, to look for an ideal, or for real love, then I'll never get married. Brr...It’s cold! Natalya Stepanovna is an excellent housekeeper, not bad-looking, well-educated. What more do I want? But I'm getting a noise in my ears from excitement. (Drinks) And it’s impossible for me not to marry. In the first place, I'm already 35— a critical age, so to speak. In the second place, I ought to lead a quiet and regular life. I suffer from palpitations, I'm excitable and always getting awfully upset; at this very moment my lips are trembling, and there’s a twitch in my right eyebrow.
Which of the following is NOT a reason why Lomov thinks he must marry?
options: (C) He is excitable and easily upset.
(D) He is in love with Natalya.
answer: (D) He is in love with Natalya.
explanation: Lomov names his critical age of thirty-five, his palpitations and his excitable nature as reasons he must marry. He praises Natalya only as an excellent housekeeper who is not bad-looking and well-educated. He never says that he is in love with her.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Lomov : He is old, but I wouldn't take five Squeezers for him. Why, how can you ? Guess is a dog; as for Squeezer, well it’s too funny to argue. Anybody you like has a dog as good as Squeezer… you may find them under every bush almost. Twenty-five roubles would be a handsome price to pay for him.
Natalya : There’s some demon of contradiction in you today, Ivan Vassilevitch. First you pretend that the Meadows are yours; now, that Guess is better than Squeezer. I don’t like people who don’t say what they mean, because you know perfectly well that Squeezer is a hundred times better than your silly Guess. Why do you want to say he isn’t ?
Lomov : I see, Natalya Stepanovna, that you consider me either blind or a fool. You must realise that Squeezer is overshot !
To pay a ‘handsome price’ most nearly means :
options: (B) to pay for a good looking dog
(C) to pay a lot of money
answer: (C) to pay a lot of money
explanation: A handsome price is a large or generous amount of money. Lomov means that even twenty-five roubles would be a lot to pay for Squeezer.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Lomov : But you can see from the documents, honoured Natalya Stepanovna. Oxen Meadows, its true were once the subject of dispute, but now everybody knows they are mine. There’s nothing to argue about. You see my aunts grandmother gave the free use of these Meadows in perpetuity to the peasants of your father’s grandfather, in return for which they were to make bricks for her. The peasants belonging to your father’s grandfather had the free use of Meadows for forty years, and had got into the habit of regarding them as their own, when it happened that……………
Natalya : No, it isn’t at all like that ! Both grandfather and great grandfather reckoned that their land extended to Burnt Marsh - which means Oxen Meadows were ours. I don’t see what there is to argue about, its simply silly.
The subject of dispute was regarding
explanation: Lomov says Oxen Meadows were once the subject of dispute but now everybody knows they are his. Natalya replies that the meadows were theirs, so the dispute is about who owns the meadows.

Bent sweetly over me.

answer:

And look up through the tree!
The sky is like a kind big smile
Bent sweetly over me.
explanation: Crow rhymes with snow, and me rhymes with tree, giving an ABAB pattern. The first option alternates while with smile and tree with me.

question:

Shook down on me
The dust of snow
From a hemlock tree
Has given my heart
A change of mood

explanation: The dust of snow is the fine powdery snow that the crow shakes down from the hemlock tree. These small particles of falling snow are snowflakes. Mist and dust of branches do not describe what falls on the poet.

subject: English Language & Literature

question:
The way a crow
Shook down on me
The dust of snow
From a hemlock tree
Has given my heart
A change of mood
The crow and the hemlock tree represent ___________.
1. sorrow
2. elation
3. hope
4. anxiety
5. enthusiasm
explanation: The crow and the hemlock tree are usually associated with gloom and ill omen. In the poem they stand for the sorrowful mood of the poet before the snow falls on him. Elation, hope and enthusiasm describe the changed mood, not these symbols.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: In the poem Dust of Snow, which negative symbols have been used to create a positive effect?
explanation: The crow and the hemlock tree are usually linked with gloom and ill omen. In the poem, the crow shaking snow from the hemlock tree changes the poet’s mood for the better.

subject: English Language & Literature

question:
And saved some part
Of a day I had rued.
Based on the above lines, select the word that describes the poet's feelings at the end of the day.
explanation: The poet had regretted the day until the crow shook down dust of snow on him. This small act saved part of the day for him. So by the end of the day he feels contented.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Some say the world will end in fire some say in ice.
From what I’ve tasted of desire
I hold with those who favour fire.
(Stanza 1)
But if it had to perish twice,
I think I know enough of hate
To say that for destruction ice
Is also great
And would suffice. (Fire and Ice)
Select the option with same rhyme scheme as lines in Stanza 1 :
options:
(A) They are all gone away,
The House is shut and still,
There is nothing more to say.

(B) Tell me not, in mournful numbers,
Life is but an empty dream!
For the soul is dead that slumbers.

(C) The dog chased the ball down the lane,
He ran with such incredible speed,
His tail was a blur, a joyful glee.

(D) The Sun is high,
The clouds drift past,
In the blue sky which is so vast.
answer:
(D) The Sun is high,
The clouds drift past,
In the blue sky which is so vast.
explanation: The first three printed lines of the extract end in ice, desire, and fire. The last two rhyme, just as past and vast rhyme in option D.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

Some say in ice.
From what I’ve tasted of desire
I hold with those who favour fire.
“Fire” and “Ice” are used in the poem as _______.
explanation: In the poem fire stands for desire and ice stands for hatred. They are implied comparisons made without like or as, which makes them metaphors.

To say that for destruction ice
Is also great
And would suffice.
The use of the word ‘perish’ corresponds best with :
explanation: To perish means to be destroyed or to come to an end. In the poem the world perishing means its destruction, which matches disintegrate, while revive and replenish mean the opposite.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Speaker's attitude towards destruction by ice
question:
But if it had to perish twice,
I think I know enough of hate
To say that for destruction ice
Is also great
And would suffice.
Which of the following best describes the speaker's attitude towards destruction caused by ice?
explanation: The speaker says that for destruction ice is also great and would suffice. Calling ice great shows that he takes its destructive power seriously and acknowledges it with a sense of awe. This is respect rather than fear, indifference or dismissal.

explanation: The poet says that for destruction ice is also great and would suffice. He thus agrees with, or supports, those who believe the world could end in ice.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Which option correctly replaces the underlined phrase in the give line from Fire and Ice? (The underlined phrase is shown in square brackets.)
I [hold with] those who favour fire.
explanation: To hold with someone means to agree with them. The poet sides with those who believe the world will end in fire.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Ice as a symbol of hatred
question: According to the poem 'Fire and Ice', some people say that the world will end in ice because humans are __________.
options: (C) passive towards the problem of climate change
explanation: In the poem, ice stands for hatred and coldness between people. Those who say the world will end in ice believe growing hatred will destroy it. Becoming spiteful towards each other reflects this hatred.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
But he’s locked in a concrete cell,
His strength behind bars,
Stalking the length of his cage,
Ignoring visitors.
What mood is created by the poet in the above lines?
explanation: The tiger is confined in a concrete cell despite his strength. The description invites sympathy and reflection on captivity.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
He should be lurking in shadow
Sliding through long grass
Near the water hole
Where the plump deer pass. (A Tiger in the Zoo)
Pick the phrase that suggests that the forest in the extract is lush.
explanation: Long grass suggests thick plant growth in the forest. The other phrases describe water, an animal, or the tiger’s action.

The few steps of his cage,
On pads of velvet quiet,
In his quiet rage.
He should be lurking in shadow,
Sliding through long grass
(A Tiger in the Zoo)
Based on the given lines from the poem, which words would best describe the feelings of the tiger ?
explanation: The tiger moves on pads of velvet quiet within the few steps of his cage, which shows him restrained and subdued. The phrase quiet rage reveals the anger he feels at his captivity.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Matching the rhyme scheme of the stanza
question:
He stalks in his vivid stripes
The few steps of his cage,
On pads of velvet quiet,
In his quiet rage.
Select the option that applies the same rhyme scheme as the lines of the given extract.
options:
(A) This bird so small and sweet,
Sings aloud in the morn,
Perched on a branch green,
Chirp, chirp, tweet, tweet.

(B) Perched on a branch green,
This bird so sweet and lean,
Sings aloud in a voice sweet,
Chirp, chirp, tweet, tweet.

(C) This bird sings without a care,
Perched on a branch green,
A song with the world to share,
With its feelings so keen.

(D) This bird so small and sweet
Sings aloud in the morn
Perched on a green branch
Singing its own melody

(A) This bird so small and sweet,
Sings aloud in the morn,
Perched on a branch green,
Chirp, chirp, tweet, tweet.
explanation: In the extract only cage and rage rhyme, while stripes and quiet stand alone. Stanza A likewise has a single rhyming pair, sweet and tweet, with two unrhymed lines. Stanza B rhymes in couplets, stanza C uses alternate rhymes and stanza D does not rhyme, so A is the closest match.

subject: English Language & Literature

answer: (B) being indifferent to visitors because it is a daily routine for him
explanation: The lines say the tiger is stalking the length of his cage and ignoring visitors. Visitors come every day in a zoo, so the caged tiger has grown indifferent to them.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

On pads of velvet quiet,
In his quiet rage

explanation: The tiger paces the few steps of his cage in his quiet rage. Rage is intense anger, here held back because he is confined. So anger best describes his feelings.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Meaning of his strength behind bars
question:
He should be snarling around houses
At the jungle’s edge,
Baring his white fangs, his claws,
Terrorising the village!

But he’s locked in a concrete cell,
His strength behind bars,
Stalking the length of his cage,
Ignoring visitors.
Which of these explains the meaning of the phrase 'His strength behind bars'?
options: (A) The tiger's strength is in its ability to break free from the cage it is in.
(B) The tiger's strength is shown when he pushes against the bars of the cage.
(C) The tiger's strength is in his resilience and ability to adapt to a new environment.
(D) The tiger's strength is confined within the bars of the cage and this makes him less threatening.
answer: (D) The tiger's strength is confined within the bars of the cage and this makes him less threatening.
explanation: The tiger is locked in a concrete cell, so his power cannot be used. His strength is imprisoned along with him, which makes the once fearsome animal harmless.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

On pads of velvet quiet,
In his quiet rage

Sliding through long grass

explanation: Pads are the soft cushioned undersides of an animal’s feet. Calling them velvet shows how softly and silently the tiger walks on its paws.

subject: English Language & Literature

question:

On pads of velvet quiet,
In his quiet rage
He should be lurking in shadow
Sliding through long grass
Near the water hole

explanation: The poet imagines the tiger in its natural home, hiding in shadow near the water hole where plump deer pass. A tiger lurks there to ambush and catch its prey.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

In his quiet rage.

Near the water hole

explanation: The tiger stalks the few steps of his cage in quiet rage. He is angry because he is confined in a cage instead of roaming free.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Feeling expressed by the caged tiger
question:

In his quiet rage.

Sliding through long grass

explanation: The phrase quiet rage shows that the caged tiger is angry. His anger comes from being confined to the few steps of his cage.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

On pads of velvet quiet
In his quiet rage.
He should be lurking in shadow
Sliding through long grass

explanation: The extract contrasts the few steps of the tiger’s cage with lurking in shadow near the water hole. The cage belongs to a zoo, while the shadows and long grass belong to the forest.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

The patrolling cars,

The epistemology of loss, how to stand up
Knowing what every man must one day know
And most know many days, how to stand up
What does the boy learn by losing the ball, according to the extract?
1) Loss is the unavoidable truth of life.
2) Material objects can be replaced.
3) Money buys happiness.
4) Losses in life can be prevented with care.
5) Life continues despite losses.
explanation: The boy learns the epistemology of loss, which every man must one day know, so loss is unavoidable. Money can replace the ball, and learning how to stand up means life goes on after loss.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Meaning of how to stand up
question:
Money is external.
He is learning, well behind his desperate eyes,
The epistemology of loss, how to stand up
Knowing what every man must one day know
And most know many days, how to stand up
The boy is learning how to stand up…
This means that he is learning to be __________ in the face of difficulties.
explanation: To stand up after a loss means to recover and carry on. The quality of bouncing back from difficulties is resilience.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Money is external.
He is learning, well behind his desperate eyes,
The epistemology of loss, how to stand up
Knowing what every man must one day know
And most know many days, how to stand up
Which option lists who is speaking these lines?
explanation: The speaker watches the boy and describes his feelings from outside, referring to him as he. The poet speaks as an observer of the boy’s grief.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Money is external.
He is learning, well behind his desperate eyes,
The epistemology of loss, how to stand up
Knowing what every man must one day know
And most know many days, how to stand up
According to the poet, from whom do we mostly learn about loss?
explanation: The poet says every man must one day know loss and most know it many days. This knowledge comes from living through losses ourselves, that is, from experience.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Boy's feelings on losing the ball
question:
Choose the option that CORRECTLY identifies what the narrator is feeling in the line given below.
As he stands rigid, trembling, staring down
(1) guilt
(2) shock
(3) shame
(4) fearlessness
(5) hopelessness
explanation: The boy stands rigid and trembling as he stares at the water where his ball has gone. This shows his shock at the sudden loss. Staring down at the water also shows his hopelessness, because the ball cannot be recovered.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
I saw it go
Merrily bouncing, down the street, and then
Merrily over — there it is in the water!
No use to say ‘O there are other balls’:
An ultimate shaking grief fixes the boy
As he stands rigid, trembling, staring down
All his young days into the harbour where
His ball went
The poet uses the ball as a symbol of the boy’s
explanation: The boy stares down all his young days into the harbour where the ball went. The lost ball stands for his carefree childhood, which can never return.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Why consoling the boy is pointless
question:
I saw it go
Merrily bouncing, down the street, and then
Merrily over — there it is in the water!
No use to say ‘O there are other balls’:
An ultimate shaking grief fixes the boy
As he stands rigid, trembling, staring down
All his young days into the harbour where
His ball went
The poet feels that there is no point consoling the boy as
options: (A) it would give him false hope.
(B) he might demand for a new ball.
(D) whatever he has lost is irretrievable.
answer: (D) whatever he has lost is irretrievable.
explanation: The poet says there is no use telling the boy there are other balls. The ball and what it represents are gone forever and cannot be recovered.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

An ultimate shaking grief fixes the boy

All his young days into the harbour where
His ball went
The word ‘harbour’ DOES NOT have a meaning similar to
explanation: A harbour is a place on the coast where ships shelter, much like a port, pier or dock. Cargo means goods carried by a ship, so it is not similar in meaning.

‘Merrily over — there it is in the water!’ The dash here is meant to convey
explanation: The ball is merrily bouncing when the dash breaks the line abruptly. The pause marks the sudden, unexpected moment when the ball falls into the water.

explanation: The poem describes the boy’s shaking grief and says he stands rigid and trembling. Worthless describes value, not a physical reaction, and does not appear in the extract.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Lesson learnt from losing the ball
question:
His ball went. I would not intrude on him;
A dime, another ball, is worthless. Now
He senses first responsibility
In a world of possessions.
The loss of the ball will help the child to understand his _______.
explanation: The extract says that now he senses first responsibility in a world of possessions. Losing the ball teaches the boy his first responsibility of learning to bear loss.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Why the speaker does not offer another ball
question:
His ball went. I would not intrude on him;
A dime, another ball, is worthless. Now
He senses first responsibility
In a world of possessions.
Giving another ball to the child is ________.
explanation: The poet says he would not intrude on the boy. Buying him another ball would interfere with the boy learning on his own how to cope with loss.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Don’t eat that chocolate, Amanda!
Remember your acne, Amanda!
Will you please look at me when I’m speaking to you,
Amanda!
How does the speaker's demand ‘look at me when I'm speaking to you' suggest the dynamic between them?
options: (A) The speaker asserts authority which has a great influence on Amanda.
(B) Amanda is defiant and the speaker feels disrespected and ignored.
(C) Amanda is interested in listening to the speaker but is distracted.
(D) The speaker feels insecure and anxious about losing Amanda.
answer: (B) Amanda is defiant and the speaker feels disrespected and ignored.
explanation: The speaker has to demand that Amanda look at her, which shows that Amanda is not paying attention. This suggests that Amanda is ignoring the instructions and the speaker feels disrespected. The speaker’s authority clearly does not have much influence, since Amanda keeps escaping into her own thoughts.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Did you finish your homework, Amanda?
Did you tidy your room, Amanda?
I thought I told you to clean your shoes,
Amanda!
(I am an orphan, roaming the street.
I pattern soft dust with my hushed, bare feet.)
What tone is conveyed through the repetition of Amanda’s name in the given extract?
explanation: The speaker repeatedly calls Amanda while listing chores she should have done. This creates a nagging tone that contrasts with Amanda’s imagined freedom.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Did you finish your homework, Amanda?
Did you tidy your room, Amanda?
I thought I told you to clean your shoes, Amanda!
(I am an orphan, roaming the street.
I pattern soft dust with my hushed, bare feet.
The silence is golden, the freedom is sweet.)
Amanda’s tone while imagining herself as an orphan is:
explanation: Amanda imagines freedom from the instructions around her. The official scheme identifies excitement in her imagined escape.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Don’t bite your nails, Amanda!
Don’t hunch your shoulders, Amanda!
Stop that slouching and sit up straight,
Amanda!
(There is a languid, emerald sea,
where the sole inhabitant is me —
a mermaid, drifting blissfully.)
What tone is conveyed through the repetition of Amanda’s name in the line ?
explanation: The repeated name follows a series of commands about her nails, her shoulders and her posture. The speaker uses Amanda’s name to correct and direct her behaviour. This gives the lines an instructive tone.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Matching the rhyme scheme of the extract
question:
Don’t bite your nails, Amanda!
Don’t hunch your shoulders, Amanda!
Stop that slouching and sit up straight,
Amanda!
(There is a languid, emerald sea,
where the sole inhabitant is me —
a mermaid, drifting blissfully.)
Select the option that applies the same rhyme scheme as the lines of the given extract.
options:
(A) Sitting by the pond
Waving my wand
Awaiting my dearest
I looked above and beyond
Awaiting my love
A sudden sound, fluttered the dove
The crackle stopped, as so did my heart

(B) Sitting by the pond
Holding tight to my bond
I looked above and beyond
Awaiting my love
I heard her come, a sudden sound
The crackle stopped, as so did my heart

(C) I sat beside the pond with her
Awaiting for her to come
I looked above and beyond
Awaiting my love
A sudden sound, I turned back
The crackle stopped, as so did my heart

(D) Sitting by the pond
Awaiting my love
I looked above and beyond
A sudden scream, I looked around
Then a shadow fell and there was no sound
The crackle stopped, as so did my heart
answer:
(A) Sitting by the pond
Waving my wand
Awaiting my dearest
I looked above and beyond
Awaiting my love
A sudden sound, fluttered the dove
The crackle stopped, as so did my heart
explanation: In the extract the first, second and fourth lines end with Amanda while the third ends with straight, giving the pattern AABA. The next two lines end with sea and me, which rhyme with each other. The seven-line poem with pond, wand, dearest and beyond follows the same AABA opening and then rhymes love with dove. The official scheme gives its rhyme scheme as AABACCD.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Why Amanda imagines herself as a mermaid
question:
Don’t bite your nails, Amanda !
Don’t hunch your shoulders, Amanda !
Stop that slouching and sit up straight, Amanda !
(“There is a languid, emerald sea,
where the sole inhabitant is me
a mermaid, drifting blissfully.”)
Amanda calls herself a mermaid because _________
options: (A) Mermaid is Amanda’s favourite fantasy character.
(B) Amanda loves watching a mermaid drifting in water.
(C) Amanda longs to be free like a mermaid which sails effortlessly in the sea.
(D) Amanda wants to sail with a mermaid in the deep-sea water.
answer: (C) Amanda longs to be free like a mermaid which sails effortlessly in the sea.
explanation: In the bracketed lines Amanda imagines herself drifting blissfully in a languid sea where she is the only inhabitant. This fantasy shows her longing to escape her mother’s constant instructions. A mermaid moving effortlessly through the sea stands for that freedom.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
(I am Rapunzel, I have not care;
life in a tower is tranquil and rare;
I’ll certainly never let down my bright hair !)
Stop that sulking at once, Amanda !
You’re always so moody, Amanda !
Anyone would think that I nagged at you,
Amanda !
(Amanda)
The tone of the speaker in the exclamation “Stop that sulking at once, Amanda !” is
1. uncertain
2. aggressive
3. dominating
4. meek
5. moody
explanation: The speaker issues a sharp command with the words at once, which sounds aggressive. She expects Amanda to obey immediately, which shows a dominating attitude. Nothing in the line suggests that the speaker is uncertain, meek or moody.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

Amanda!

life in a tower is tranquil and rare;)
Complete the sentence with the appropriate option.
“Will you please look at me when I’m speaking to you, Amanda!” tells us that the mother’s attitude is __________.
explanation: The mother keeps issuing commands and demands that Amanda look at her while she speaks. This controlling and insistent tone is authoritative. Nothing in the line sounds relaxed, loving or thoughtful.

subject: English Language & Literature

Don’t eat that chocolate, Amanda!
Which of the following best describes the symbolic meaning of the soft dust and hushed, bare feet in Amanda's orphan daydream?
options: (A) A sense of isolation and loneliness
explanation: Amanda imagines roaming the street quietly with nobody to instruct her. The same stanza ends by saying the freedom is sweet, so the imagery stands for freedom and independence.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

The Speaker’s tone is
explanation: The speaker keeps telling Amanda what to do and what not to do, such as not eating chocolate and remembering her acne. These repeated directions give the lines an instructive tone.

Amanda’s mother is continuously __________ Amanda.
explanation: Every line spoken by the mother scolds or corrects Amanda. Reprimanding means rebuking someone, which matches her constant criticism.

Which word in the extract is opposite in meaning to the word ‘dull’ ?
explanation: Dull means lacking brightness or shine. Bright, used in the line about never letting down her bright hair, is its opposite.

Which of these reflects the speaker’s tone in the second stanza of the extract?
1. critical
2. worried
3. concerned
4. sympathetic
5. commanding
explanation: The speaker orders Amanda to stop sulking at once, which is commanding. Calling her always so moody is critical rather than sympathetic.

Identify the reason Amanda says she will never let down her hair.
options: (B) She likes her hair a lot.
(C) She wishes to be left alone.
answer: (C) She wishes to be left alone.
explanation: In the fairy tale, Rapunzel lets down her hair so that others can climb up to her. By refusing to do so, Amanda shows she wants to stay undisturbed in her peaceful tower.

Stop that sulking at once, Amanda!

Select the sentence in which the word ‘bright’ is used in a similar manner as line 3 of the extract.
options: (A) Sekhar is a very bright child.
(B) Rama looked bright and chirpy today.
(C) Bobby's shirt was so bright and cheerful.
(D) Hemant has such bright prospects for the future.
answer: (C) Bobby's shirt was so bright and cheerful.
explanation: In my bright hair, the word describes a vivid, shining colour. A bright shirt uses the same sense, while the other sentences mean clever, lively or promising.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Listen. The glass is breaking.
The trees are stumbling forward
into the night. Winds rush to meet them.
The moon is broken like a mirror,
its pieces flash now in the crown of the tallest oak.
Choose the correct option to complete the sentence.
The phrase ‘stumbling forward’ suggests that the trees’ movement is ________.
explanation: To stumble is to move forward unsteadily and almost fall. The trees are leaving the house for the first time, so their movement is awkward and uncertain rather than graceful or controlled.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
I sit inside, doors open to the veranda
writing long letters
in which I scarcely mention the departure
of the forest from the house.
The night is fresh, the whole moon shines
in a sky still open
the smell of leaves and lichen
still reaches like a voice into the rooms. (Trees)
What kind of atmosphere is created through the given extract ? Select the correct option(s) : 1. nostalgia 2. serenity 3. detachment 4. loss 5. joy
explanation: The fresh night, moonlight, and the smell of leaves create a peaceful mood. The return of the trees to the forest also suggests joy.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
“All night the roots work
To disengage themselves from the cracks
in the veranda floor. The leaves strain towards the glass
small twigs stiff with exertion
long-cramped boughs shuffling
under the roof
like newly discharged patients
half dazed, moving to the clinic doors (Trees)
The phrase ‘half-dazed’ is used for the branches as they adjust from being indoors to being in the open. It highlights the branches’ :
explanation: The simile compares the moving branches to recently discharged patients. Half-dazed suggests their disorientation and fragility as they move outside.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The leaves strain toward the glass
small twigs stiff with exertion
long-cramped boughs shuffling under the roof
like newly discharged patients
half-dazed, moving
to the clinic doors.
Complete the sentence with the appropriate option.
The imagery and descriptions in the poem create a mood of ______________________ .
explanation: The trees strain toward the glass and the boughs shuffle like newly discharged patients moving to the clinic doors. This shows the trees in the middle of moving out of the house toward the forest. Their half-dazed movement adds a sense of uncertainty.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
I sit inside, doors open to the veranda writing long letters in which I scarcely mention the departure of the forest from the house. The night is fresh, the whole moon shines in a sky still open ......
How does the poet describe the night ?
1. dark 2. frightening 3. dense 4. fresh 5. bright
Select the correct option :
explanation: The poet says that the night is fresh and the whole moon shines in a sky still open. A full, shining moon makes the night bright. The lines do not describe the night as dark, frightening or dense.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
My head is full of whispers
which tomorrow will be silent.
Listen. The glass is breaking.
The trees are stumbling forward
into the night. Winds rush to meet them.
The moon is broken like a mirror,
its pieces flash now in the crown
of the tallest oak.
(The Trees)
What is the mood or atmosphere conveyed by the imagery in the passage ?
explanation: The images of breaking glass, trees stumbling forward into the night and a moon broken like a mirror create an unsettling scene. The whispers that will be silent tomorrow hint that something is about to change. Together these details give the extract an eerie and foreboding atmosphere.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

The trees are stumbling forward
into the night. Winds rush to meet them.
The moon is broken like a mirror,

of the tallest Oak.
Complete the sentence with the appropriate option. In the third line, the word ‘Listen’ is used to _______.
options: (A) serve no purpose but to complete the sentence.
(B) emphasize listening carefully to the sound of glass breaking.
(C) emphasize listening carefully as a change is about to take place.
answer: (C) emphasize listening carefully as a change is about to take place.
explanation: Listen is a command that draws attention to the sounds of the trees breaking free from the house. These sounds signal that a major change is about to happen, so the poet stresses careful listening.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The trees inside are moving out into the forest,
the forest that was empty all these days
where no bird could sit
no insect hide
no sun bury its feet in shadow
the forest that was empty all these nights
will be full of trees by morning.
The poet has used a poetic device in the given lines. What effect does she wish to create by its use?
…no bird could sit
no insect hide
no sun…
explanation: The word no is repeated at the start of successive lines. This repetition emphasises how completely empty and lifeless the forest was without trees.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The trees inside are moving out into the forest,
the forest that was empty all these days
where no bird could sit
no insect hide
no sun bury its feet in shadow
the forest that was empty all these nights
will be full of trees by morning.
Select the appropriate option to complete the sentence, according to the extract.
The idea of a forest that has been ‘empty all these days’ is _________.
explanation: A forest is naturally full of trees, birds and insects. A forest without trees, where no bird can sit and no insect can hide, goes against nature.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The trees inside are moving out into the forest,
the forest that was empty all these days
where no bird could sit
no insect hide
no sun bury its feet in shadow
the forest that was empty all these nights
will be full of trees by morning.
How does the use of enjambment impact this extract?
explanation: Enjambment carries a sentence from one line to the next without a pause. The lines flow on continuously, building momentum like the trees steadily moving out into the forest.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
..........Winds rush to meet them.
The moon is broken like a mirror,
Its pieces flash now in the crown
of the tallest oak.
The above lines were written by
explanation: These lines come from the poem The Trees. The poem was written by Adrienne Rich, while Robert Frost wrote Dust of Snow and Fire and Ice.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Meaning of the crown of the oak
question:
..........Winds rush to meet them.
The moon is broken like a mirror,
Its pieces flash now in the crown
of the tallest oak.
The crown of the oak lies in its
explanation: The crown of a tree is its uppermost part made of the top branches. The broken moon flashes in the crown of the tallest oak, that is, among its highest branches.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The trees inside are moving out into the forest,
the forest that was empty all these days
where no bird could sit
no insect hide
no sun bury its feet in shadow
the forest that was empty all these nights
will be full of trees by morning.
All these days, the forest referred to here was _________ .
explanation: The extract twice describes the forest as empty all these days and nights. No bird could sit and no insect could hide there because it had no trees.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Figure of speech in the extract
question:
The trees inside are moving out into the forest,
the forest that was empty all these days
where no bird could sit
no insect hide
no sun bury its feet in shadow
the forest that was empty all these nights
will be full of trees by morning.
The figure of speech used in these lines is _________ .
explanation: The trees are shown moving out into the forest as if they were living beings. The sun is also given feet to bury in shadow, so human qualities are given to non-human things.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The fog comes
on little cat feet.
It sits looking
over harbour and city
on silent haunches
and then moves on.
On the basis of the extract, select the correct option. The image of a cat moving “on little cat feet” evokes:
explanation: The comparison makes fog seem quiet and gentle. A cats soft steps support the image of softness.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
The fog comes
on little cat feet.
It sits looking
over harbour and city
on silent haunches
and then moves on.
Complete the sentence with the appropriate option.
The lines from the poem tell us that the city is ______.
explanation: The fog sits looking over harbour and city. A harbour is a sheltered place for ships on the coast, so the city must be coastal. The lines give no hint of hills, industry or under-development.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
Belinda embraced him, Mustard licked him,
No one mourned for his pirate victim.
Ink and Blink in glee did gyrate
Around the dragon that ate the pirate. (The Tale of Custard the Dragon)
‘Embraced’ in this context means :
options: (C) to put your arms around someone
answer: (C) to put your arms around someone
explanation: Belinda embraces Custard after his victory. Embraced means putting her arms around him.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
Belinda embraced him, Mustard licked him,
No one mourned for his pirate victim.
Ink and Blink in glee did gyrate
Around the dragon that ate the pirate. (The Tale of Custard the Dragon)
Select the option that applies the same rhyme scene as the lines of the given extract.
options:
(A) I have a cat
I have a house
I have a mouse
I have a hat.

(B) She went there
The house was bare
Not a sound was heard
Except the tweet of a bird.

(C) People along the sand
all turn to look one way.
The wetter ground like glass
swept their gaze away.

(D) The bird flew
to the sky blue
It was beauty true
I have to say
answer:
(B) She went there
The house was bare
Not a sound was heard
Except the tweet of a bird.
explanation: The extract pairs its first two line endings and then its last two. There and bare, followed by heard and bird, use the same AABB pattern.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
Belinda giggled till she shook the house,

Ink and Mustard rudely asked his age,
When Custard cried for a nice safe cage.
Suddenly, suddenly they heard a nasty sound,
And Mustard growled, and they all looked around.
What inference can be drawn from the repetition of ‘suddenly, suddenly’ in the above extract ?
options: (C) It emphasises that an unexpected noise was heard
(D) It directs our notice to Mustard’s growling
answer: (C) It emphasises that an unexpected noise was heard
explanation: The word suddenly is repeated in the line that introduces the nasty sound. The repetition stresses how abruptly and unexpectedly the noise broke into the teasing. Mustard growls only after this sound is heard.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:

options:

which she thought was very far

and felt the crumple of the sand.

She stretched her hand
As it was very far
But felt the crumble of the sand.

Which she thought was very far
Her hand she stretched
But felt the crumble of the sand.

(D) Through the telescope she saw a star

Her hand she stretched afar

which she thought was very far
She stretched her hand
and felt the crumple of the sand.
explanation: The first four lines of the extract end with house, mouse, age and cage, giving the rhyme scheme AABB. The first option ends with star, far, hand and sand, which follows the same AABB pattern. The other options give ABAB, AABC or AAAB instead.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
Belinda paled, and she cried Help! Help!
But Mustard fled with a terrified yelp,
Ink trickled down to the bottom of the household,
And little mouse Blink strategically mouseholed.
What kind of atmosphere is created through these lines?
Select the correct option
1. Urgency 2. Apprehension 3. Uncertainty 4. mystery 5. Aggression
explanation: Belinda cries for help and Mustard flees with a terrified yelp, which creates urgency. Ink and Blink hide in fear, adding apprehension and uncertainty about what will happen next. The lines show neither aggression nor any mystery.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
Belinda was as brave as a barrel full of bears,
And Ink and Blink chased lions down the stairs,
Mustard was as brave as a tiger in a rage,
But Custard cried for a nice safe cage.
Which of the following best describes the theme of the poem ?
explanation: Belinda and her pets boast of being brave, while Custard is mocked as a coward. When the pirate attacks, the boasters run away and only Custard fights. The crisis shows the true character of each of them.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
Belinda paled, and she cried Help ! Help !
But Mustard fled with a terrified yelp,
Ink trickled down to the bottom of the household,
And little mouse Blink strategically mouseholed.
‘Help ! Help ! is an example of :
explanation: The word Help is used twice in a row as Belinda cries out. Deliberately repeating a word for emphasis is the poetic device called repetition.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
Belinda paled, and she cried Help ! Help !
But Mustard fled with a terrified yelp,
Ink trickled down to the bottom of the household,
And little mouse Blink strategically mouseholed.
The phrase ‘trickled down’ means ____________ .
explanation: To trickle is to flow or move slowly in small amounts. The line shows Ink creeping slowly down to the bottom of the household out of fear.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
Belinda embraced him, Mustard licked him,
No one mourned for his pirate victim.
Ink and Blink in glee did gyrate
Around the dragon that ate the pirate.
Belinda embraced Mustard
I. out of shock
II. out of helplessness
III. out of happiness
IV. out of gratitude
Choose the correct option :
explanation: After Custard ate the pirate, the whole household rejoiced that the danger had passed. The official scheme treats the embrace as an expression of happiness.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
Belinda embraced him, Mustard licked him,
No one mourned for his pirate victim.
Ink and Blink in glee did gyrate
Around the dragon that ate the pirate.
The phrase ‘no one mourned’ most nearly means
options: (D) no one paid a tribute to him
explanation: To mourn is to feel or show sorrow for someone who has died. No one mourned means that no one felt sad for the pirate.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question:
But the dragon was a coward, and she called him Custard.
Custard the dragon had big sharp teeth,
And spikes on top of him and scales underneath
Mouth like a fireplace, chimney for a nose,
And realio, trulio daggers on his toes.
Which one of the following is not a feature of the Dragon ?
options: (D) could release fire from the mouth
explanation: The extract begins by saying the dragon was a coward, which is why Belinda called him Custard. Being brave as a lion is therefore not one of his features, while his teeth, spikes and fiery mouth are described.

subject: English Language & Literature
topic: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
subtopic: Effect of the simile mouth like a fireplace
question:
But the dragon was a coward, and she called him Custard.
Custard the dragon had big sharp teeth,
And spikes on top of him and scales underneath
Mouth like a fireplace, chimney for a nose,
And realio, trulio daggers on his toes.
What effect does the poet want to create by the simile ‘mouth like a fireplace’ ?
explanation: Comparing the mouth to a fireplace stresses how fierce and fiery the dragon looks. The simile emphasises his frightening appearance, which contrasts with his cowardly nature.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Reason for wanting to dye her hair
question:
But I can get a hair-dye
And set such colour there,
Brown, or black, or carrot,
That young men in despair
May love me for myself alone
And not my yellow hair.”
Identify the reason for the speaker’s need to colour her hair, as per the extract.
options: (A) Her control over what makes her look beautiful.
(B) Her desire to be loved for inner beauty
(C) Her need to change people’s perception about beauty
(D) Her conviction that she is beautiful inside
answer: (D) Her conviction that she is beautiful inside
explanation: The speaker wants young men to love her for herself alone and not her yellow hair. The official scheme reads this as her conviction that her true beauty lies within her.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
But I can get a hair-dye
And set such colour there,
Brown, or black, or carrot,
That young men in despair
May love me for myself alone
And not my yellow hair.”
Select the sentence in which the word ‘set’ is used in the similar manner as line 2 of the extract.
options: (A) I want to set him up and get my work done this time.
(B) Do you have another set of the books that I can read?
(C) The dessert needs to set for two hours before being served.
(D) The set for the school play looked quite grand.
answer: (C) The dessert needs to set for two hours before being served.
explanation: In line 2, to set colour in the hair means to make it fixed and lasting. A dessert that needs to set becomes firm and fixed in the same sense.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Comparison used for the lady’s hair
question:
“Never shall a young man,
Thrown into despair
By those great honey-coloured
Ramparts at your ear,
Love you for yourself alone
And not your yellow hair.”
The lady’s hair is compared to __________ .
explanation: The poet describes the lady’s hair as great honey-coloured ramparts at her ear. Ramparts are protective walls, and the image shows her thick hair framing her face. Honey only describes the colour of the hair.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Reason for the young man’s love
question:
“Never shall a young man,
Thrown into despair
By those great honey-coloured
Ramparts at your ear,
Love you for yourself alone
And not your yellow hair.”
The young man has fallen in love with the lady for her ___________ .
explanation: The young man is thrown into despair by her honey-coloured hair. The poem says he loves her for her yellow hair, which is part of her looks, and not for herself alone.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Reason for the vet’s advance plan
question:
Tricki was tottering along in his little tweed coat.... He struggled on, drooping in his harness. I thought it wouldn’t be long before I heard from Mrs. Pumphrey. The expected call came within a few days. Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught. Tricki would eat nothing. Refused even his favourite dishes; and besides, he had bouts of vomiting. He spent all his time lying on a rug, panting. Didn’t want to go for walks, didn’t want to do anything. I had made my plans in advance. The only way was to get Tricki out of the house for a period. I suggested that he be hospitalized for about a fortnight to be kept under observation. The poor lady almost swooned. She was sure he would pine and die if he did not see her every day. But I took a firm line. Tricki was very ill and this was the only way to save him.
Why had the author made his plans in advance ?
options: (A) Mrs. Pumphrey was worried that Tricki would pine and die without her.
(B) The author was aware of the severity of Tricki’s medical condition.
(C) The author knew about Mrs. Pumphrey’s financial condition.
(D) The author had planned his own vacation.
answer: (B) The author was aware of the severity of Tricki’s medical condition.
explanation: The author had already seen Tricki tottering and struggling in his harness and expected a call about him. He knew Tricki was very ill and that taking him out of the house was the only way to save him. His plan came from understanding how serious the condition was.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:

I had made my plans in advance. The only way was to get Tricki out of the house for a period. I suggested that he be hospitalised for about a fortnight to be kept under observation.
Which of the following is not a reason why Mr. Herriot thinks Tricki needs to be taken out of the house for a period ?
options: (A) He wanted to keep Tricki away from Mrs. Pumphrey.
(B) He wanted to keep Tricki under observation.
(C) He wanted to do an experiment on Tricki.
(D) He wanted to improve Tricki’s health.
answer: (C) He wanted to do an experiment on Tricki.
explanation: Herriot wanted Tricki away from his indulgent owner, kept under observation and restored to health. Nothing in the story suggests that he planned an experiment on the dog. So doing an experiment is not one of his reasons.

question:

I had made my plans in advance. The only way was to get Tricki out of the house for a period. I suggested that he be hospitalised for about a fortnight to be kept under observation.
Which of the following best describes Mrs. Pumphrey ?
explanation: Tricki’s owner loves the dog dearly and is distraught when he falls ill, which shows compassion. Her constant overfeeding and pampering caused his illness, which shows she is impractical. The other pairs of traits do not match her behaviour in the story.

subject: English Language & Literature
question: What does the exclamation, “This is a triumph of surgery!”, by Mrs. Pumphrey, mean?
options: (B) The mistress could take back her pet.
(C) The doctor was a great veterinarian.
explanation: Tricki was never operated upon and recovered only through the strict diet and exercise planned by the narrator. Mrs Pumphrey’s exclamation shows that this planned treatment had succeeded.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
It was a temptation to keep Tricki on as a permanent guest,...
Why did Mr Herriot NOT give in to the temptation to keep Tricki at the surgery in 'A Triumph of Surgery'?
options: (A) He could not afford to take care of Tricki.
(B) He felt Tricki would be unhappy at the surgery.
(C) He knew Mrs Pumphrey was miserable without Tricki.
(D) He continued feasting on items Mrs Pumphrey sent for Tricki.
answer: (C) He knew Mrs Pumphrey was miserable without Tricki.
explanation: Mrs Pumphrey kept phoning for news of Tricki and was miserable while he was away. Mr Herriot knew how much she was suffering without her dog. So once Tricki recovered, he did not keep him any longer.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Purpose of the list of Tricki's belongings
question:
...maids rushed in and out bringing his day bed, his night bed, favourite cushions, toys and rubber rings, breakfast bowl, lunch bowl, supper bowl.
Mr Herriot gives the above description in the story 'A Triumph of Surgery' to show how __________.
options: (B) difficult it was to keep Tricki healthy
(C) privileged and rich Mrs Pumphrey was
(D) important Mrs Pumphrey was as a client
explanation: Tricki arrives with two beds, cushions, toys and a separate bowl for every meal. This long list shows how pampered and spoilt he was by Mrs Pumphrey.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
I think he knew I made a little money this way but he did not seem to mind. Anil made money by fits and starts. He would borrow one week, lend the next. He kept worrying about his next cheque, but as soon as it arrived, he would go out and celebrate. It seems he wrote for magazines – a queer way to make a living’ ! One evening he came home with a small bundle of notes, saying he had just sold a book to a publisher. At night I saw him tuck the money under the mattress. I had been working for Anil for almost a month and apart from cheating on the shopping, had not done anything in my line of work. (The Thief’s Story)
Complete the following sentence. Anil made money by ‘fits and starts’ means that he _______.
options: (A) deemed it fit to start investing money.
(B) started earning money in the recent past.
(D) put his money to use frequently.
explanation: Anil did not receive money on a regular schedule. The phrase describes income arriving intermittently.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Value of education for Hari Singh
question:
Later, he patted me on the head and said never mind, he’d teach me to cook. He also taught me to write my name and said he would soon teach me to write whole sentences and to add numbers. I was grateful. I knew that once I could write like an educated man there would be no limit to what I could achieve.
It was quite pleasant working for Anil. I made the tea in the morning and then would take my time buying the day’s supplies, usually making a profit of about a rupee a day. I think he knew I made a little money this way but he did not seem to mind.
(The Thief’s Story)
Which of the following best describes the realization Hari Singh had while working for Anil ?
options: (A) that he would become a rich person one day
(B) that Anil was a very intelligent master but a miser
(C) that he would be able to accomplish a lot if he gets educated
(D) that Anil made a lot of money from his job
answer: (C) that he would be able to accomplish a lot if he gets educated
explanation: Hari Singh says that once he could write like an educated man there would be no limit to what he could achieve. This shows his realization that education would help him accomplish a great deal.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Feeling unlikely on seeing the note
question:
There was a fifty rupee note between his fingers. My heart sank. I thought I had been discovered. “I made some money yesterday,” he explained. “Now you’ll be paid regularly.” My spirits rose. But when I took the note, I saw it was still wet from the night’s rain. “Today we’ll start writing sentences,” he said.
He knew. But neither his lips nor his eyes showed anything.
(The Thief’s Story)
In the context of the given extract :
What was the feelings UNLIKELY to have been on seeing ‘a fifty rupee note between his fingers’ ?
explanation: On seeing the note the narrator says his heart sank because he thought he had been discovered. He felt worried and unhappy, not joyful. His spirits rose only later, when Anil said he would be paid regularly.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Reason Hari Singh cannot learn to write
question:
I went back to the bazaar and sat down in the shelter of the clock tower. The clock showed midnight. I felt for the notes. They were damp from the rain.
Anil’s Money. In the morning he would probably have given me two or three rupees to go to the cinema, but now I had it all.
I couldn’t cook his meals, run to the bazaar, or learn to write whole sentences any more.
I had forgotten about them in the excitement of the theft. Whole sentences, I knew, could one day bring me more than a few hundred rupees. It was a simple matter to steal- and sometimes just as simple to be caught.
Which of the following is NOT a reason why Hari Singh thinks he would not be able to write whole sentences ?
options: (A) Anil would not be there to teach him.
(B) He had robbed Anil and left.
(C) He would not go back to Anil to learn.
(D) He had no money to take admission in school.
answer: (D) He had no money to take admission in school.
explanation: Hari Singh feels he can no longer learn to write whole sentences because he has robbed Anil and run away. Without Anil there is no one to teach him. The extract never mentions school admission or a lack of money for it.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
I followed casually.
“Hello again,” he said.
I gave him my most appealing smile. “I want to work for you,” I said.
“But I can’t pay you.”
I thought that over for a minute. Perhaps I had misjudged my man. I asked, “Can you feed me?”
“Can you cook?”
“I can cook,” I lied again.
“If you can cook, then maybe I can feed you.”
He took me to his room over the Jumna Sweet Shop and told me I could sleep on the balcony. But the meal I cooked that night must have been terrible because Anil gave it to a stray dog and told me to be off. But I just hung around, smiling in my most appealing way, and he couldn’t help laughing.
Even though Hari Singh followed Anil casually, it was a/an …………………
explanation: Hari Singh only pretended to be casual while following Anil. He had already marked Anil as an easy target, so the move was planned and staged.

question: Anil’s carelessness made stealing from him __________ for Hari Singh.
explanation: Hari Singh says it is hard to rob a careless man because he often does not even notice the theft. This takes all the pleasure out of the work, so stealing from Anil was uninteresting.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Meaning of getting into someone's confidence
question:
I was still a thief when I met Anil. And though only 15, I was an experienced and fairly successful hand. Anil was watching a wrestling match when I approached him. He was about 25; a tall, lean fellow; and he looked easy-going, kind and simple enough for my purpose. I hadn't had much luck of late and thought I might be able to get into the young man's confidence.
"You look a bit of a wrestler yourself," I said. A little flattery helps in making friends.
"So do you," he replied, which put me off for a moment because at that time I was rather thin.
"Well," I said modestly, "I do wrestle a bit."
"What's your name?"
"Hari Singh," I lied. I took a new name every month. That kept me ahead of the police and my former employers.
I might be able to get into the young man’s confidence.
Based on the line above, we can say that Hari wanted to __________.
options: (A) reduce Anil's confidence to dupe him
(C) gain Anil's trust to exploit him
answer: (C) gain Anil's trust to exploit him
explanation: To get into someone's confidence means to win their trust. Hari was a thief, so he wanted to win Anil's trust in order to rob him later.

options: (A) The profits of our company have grown modestly over the last year.
(B) Ryan always modestly shrugs off the compliments from people.
(C) We're looking to buy a modestly furnished apartment.

answer: (B) Ryan always modestly shrugs off the compliments from people.
explanation: In the extract, Hari modestly says that he wrestles a bit, playing down his own ability. Ryan modestly shrugging off compliments uses the word in the same sense of not boasting. The other sentences use modestly to mean moderately, simply or decently.

subject: English Language & Literature
question:
Ausable did not fit any description of a secret agent Fowler had ever read. Following him down the musty corridor of the gloomy French hotel where Ausable had a room, Fowler felt let down. It was a small room, on the sixth and top floor and scarcely a setting for a romantic adventure. Ausable was, for one thing, fat, very fat. And then there was his accent. Though he spoke French and German passably, he had never altogether lost the American accent he had brought to Paris from Boston twenty years ago. “You are disappointed,” Ausable said wheezily over his shoulder. (The Midnight Visitor)
Which of the following describes how Fowler felt on seeing Ausable for the first time ?
explanation: Fowler expected a romantic and impressive spy. Ausable and his gloomy hotel instead left him surprised and disappointed.

subject: English Language & Literature
subtopic: Reason for Ausable’s irritation about the balcony
question:
“It’s not my balcony,” Ausable said with extreme irritation. “It belongs to the next apartment.” He glanced explanatorily at Fowler. “You see,” he said, “this room used to be part of a large unit, and the next room — through that door there — used to be the living room. It had the balcony, which extends under my window now. You can get onto it from the empty room two doors down — and somebody did, last month. The management promised to block it off. But they haven’t.”
Which of the following was the reason that irritated Ausable about the balcony ?
options: (B) its location relative to his apartment
(C) its accessibility from the neighbouring unit
(D) its maintenance by the apartment management
answer: (C) its accessibility from the neighbouring unit
explanation: Ausable explains that the balcony can be reached from the empty room two doors down. He adds that somebody got onto it last month and the management has not blocked it off. His irritation comes from this easy access from the neighbouring unit.

question:

Ausable was, for one thing, fat. Very fat. And then there was his accent. Though he spoke French and German passably, he had never altogether lost the American accent he had brought to Paris from Boston twenty years ago.
“You are disappointed,” Ausable said wheezily over his shoulder. “You were told that I was a secret agent, a spy, dealing in espionage and danger. You wished to meet me because you are a writer, young and romantic. You envisioned mysterious figures in the night, the crack of pistols, drugs in the wine.”
Which of these means the same as 'romantic' in the line below?
It was a small room, on the sixth and top floor, and scarcely a setting for a romantic adventure.
explanation: Fowler expected the thrilling, mysterious life of a spy. Here romantic means full of excitement and adventure, so exciting is the closest meaning.

Who is Max ?
explanation: Max is a rival secret agent who enters Ausable’s room with a pistol. He has come to steal the report about new missiles, which shows he is a spy.
